title: Insulin Dose-Adjusted Hemoglobin A1c Has Suboptimal Performance for Identifying C-Peptide-Defined Partial Remission: The SEARCH for Diabetes in Youth Study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Insulin dose-adjusted hemoglobin A1c (IDAA1c = HbA1c [%] + [4 × total daily dose in units/kg/day]) ≤9 is widely used to define partial remission in pediatric type 1 diabetes and as an eligibility criterion or outcome in disease-modifying therapy trials. However, it has not been validated in U.S. youth. Because higher BMI increases insulin resistance and insulin requirements, we hypothesized that IDAA1c would perform suboptimally in participants with overweight or obesity.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed data from 422 SEARCH for Diabetes in Youth study participants with mixed-meal tolerance test (MMTT)-stimulated C-peptide within 12 months of diagnosis. Partial remission was defined using MMTT-stimulated area under the curve (AUC) mean C-peptide. Participant characteristics were compared by BMI category (<85th percentile [normal or underweight] and ≥85th percentile [overweight or obese]) using Wilcoxon rank sum and Fisher exact tests. Sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) AUC of IDAA1c ≤9 for identifying partial remission were evaluated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Participants with normal or underweight versus participants with overweight or obesity had lower IDAA1c (8.95 vs. 9.28, P = 0.043) despite lower stimulated C-peptide (1.25 vs. 1.88 ng/mL, P < 0.001). Overall, IDAA1c ≤9 had 61% sensitivity and 79% specificity for predicting C-peptide ≥0.91 ng/mL with an ROC AUC of 0.77. Among participants with overweight or obesity, sensitivity was 45% and specificity 81%. A Youden index-derived cutoff of IDAA1c ≤11.6 improved sensitivity to 93%, with specificity of 54% in participants with overweight or obesity.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: IDAA1c ≤9 demonstrated suboptimal accuracy as a screening test for partial remission, especially underestimating β-cell function in youth with overweight or obesity. BMI-specific cutoffs improved sensitivity but reduced specificity.

title: Safety of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and other new-generation glucose-lowering agents for the management of type 2 diabetes in pregnancy: a French nationwide population-based study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) and other second-line glucose-lowering agents are increasingly used among women of reproductive age. Data on the safety of these medications in pregnancy are limited. We aimed to assess the comparative safety of first-trimester exposure to second-line glucose-lowering agents on the risk of organ-specific congenital malformations among pregnancies affected by type 2 diabetes mellitus that was pharmacologically treated.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a population-based cohort study using the French National Health Data System including singleton infants born after pregnancies lasting more than 22 weeks, in women aged 18 to 50 years with pregestational, pharmacologically treated type 2 diabetes from January 2011 to August 2024. We defined first-trimester exposure to glucose-lowering agents as having at least one prescription filled from 30 days before through to 91 days after conception. All glucose-lowering agents were considered: insulin, metformin, GLP-1RA, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4i), sulfonylureas and other glucose-lowering agents. The primary reference group was the use of insulin alone, but the use of metformin, with and without insulin, and non-use of glucose-lowering agents were also comparators in additional analyses to facilitate comparison with previous studies. Analysed outcomes were major congenital malformations during the delivery stay and up to 1 year after birth to consider delayed identification, using ICD-10 codes as per EUROCAT (European surveillance of congenital anomalies) guidelines. Adjusted RRs and 95% CIs were estimated using Poisson regressions with generalised estimating equations. Values of BMI and HbA1c were unavailable in the database; proxies of diabetes severity were used instead for confounding adjustment.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 19,092 eligible pregnancies, 17.5% were exposed to insulin alone, 34.7% to at least one second-line glucose-lowering agent and 10.4% were unexposed to any glucose-lowering agent during the first trimester. Compared with insulin-only use, first-trimester exposure to second-line glucose-lowering agents was not associated with an increased risk of overall or organ-specific major congenital malformations. Sensitivity analyses using stricter exposure definitions suggested a possible small increased risk of cardiac malformations following first-trimester exposure to GLP-1 RA and sulfonylureas.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: In this largest study to date on the use of glucose-lowering agents in pregnancy, first-trimester exposure to second-line glucose-lowering agents was not associated with an increased risk of major congenital malformations when compared with insulin-only use. However, a small increased risk of cardiac defects associated with first-trimester exposure to GLP-1RA and sulfonylureas is possible, and thus teratogenicity cannot be excluded.

title: Increased Risk of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Poor Sleep Quality Among Older Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: The DCCT/EDIC Study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To investigate the prevalence of sleep problems and their risk factors among older adults with type 1 diabetes.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: Participants with type 1 diabetes in the Diabetes Control and Complications Trial/Epidemiology of Diabetes Interventions and Complications (DCCT/EDIC) study completed validated questionnaires to assess sleep-related problems, including risk of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) (intermediate/high risk: STOP-Bang ≥3), poor sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index >5), and mild or greater levels of excessive daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale >10). Logistic regression models assessed the odds of each sleep problem by demographic and clinical variables, glycemia, and diabetes complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In 963 participants (52% male, mean [SD] age 64 [7] years) with type 1 diabetes (mean [SD] duration 43 [5] years), diagnosed OSA and current positive airway pressure device use were reported by 29% and 19% of participants, respectively. Increased OSA risk was present in 64%, poor sleep quality in 43%, and daytime sleepiness in 10% of participants. Each 1% absolute increase (11 mmol/mol) in current or mean HbA1c was associated with 15% to 20% higher odds of any sleep problem. In models adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and mean HbA1c, cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy was associated with higher odds of intermediate/high OSA risk, and albuminuria and severe hypoglycemia were associated with higher odds of poor sleep quality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: OSA risk and poor sleep quality were common among DCCT/EDIC participants. Sleep assessments for older individuals with long-standing type 1 diabetes and research to identify mechanisms to explain the observed associations are warranted.

title: Disease modification outcomes in type 2 diabetes: a modified Delphi.
type_basis: PubMed文献类型：Journal Article,Review

abstract.text: Type 2 diabetes is a heterogeneous, progressive chronic condition for which management has traditionally focused on glycaemic control and cardiovascular risk factors, rather than focusing on altering long-term disease trajectory. Increasing evidence indicates that progression and complications might be modifiable, but the absence of a core outcome set for disease modification limits trial design and intervention comparison. To address this gap, we developed a core outcome set for disease modification in type 2 diabetes through a modified Delphi process conducted according to COMET guidance. Candidate outcomes were identified from the literature and refined by an international multidisciplinary steering group comprising clinicians, researchers, and people living with type 2 diabetes. Across two Delphi rounds involving health-care professionals, researchers, and patients (round one n=233; round two n=79), agreement was reached for 35 outcomes spanning 11 domains. This framework aims to support outcome selection, consistency across trials, comparison of interventions, and evaluation of disease-modifying strategies in type 2 diabetes.

title: Petrelintide, a human amylin analogue for the treatment of obesity (ZUPREME 1): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
type_basis: PubMed研究类型：Journal Article,Randomized Controlled Trial,Clinical Trial, Phase II,Multicenter Study

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Petrelintide is a novel, long-acting amylin analogue being developed for long-term treatment of obesity, leveraging a mechanism of action distinct from incretin-based treatments. This phase 2 trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly petrelintide versus placebo in people with obesity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involved 32 sites (public hospitals and private clinics) in Poland, Romania, and the USA. Adults aged at least 18 years without type 2 diabetes, with a BMI of at least 30 kg/m2 or with a BMI of at least 27 kg/m2 with hypertension or dyslipidaemia, or both, were randomly assigned (5:1) to self-administered subcutaneous injections of once-weekly maintenance doses of petrelintide (1·0-9·0 mg) or placebo for 42 weeks including dose escalation. Randomisation was done via a central interactive response technology system and was stratified by MRI participation. Participants, trial staff, and the study funder were masked to treatment assignment but not to different maintenance doses; masking was maintained by use of identical vials for petrelintide and placebo. The primary endpoint was percentage change in bodyweight from baseline after 28 weeks. Analyses included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose. Missing data were assumed to be missing at random. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06662539) and the Clinical Trials Information System (2024-512549-18) and was completed on Mar 7, 2026.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: From Dec 9, 2024, to Feb 25, 2025, we screened 714 participants, of whom 493 were randomly assigned and 485 received at least one dose of petrelintide or placebo. 79 participants received at least one dose of treatment with petrelintide 1·0 mg, 81 with petrelintide 2·5 mg, 83 with petrelintide 5·0 mg, 79 with petrelintide 7·0 mg, 82 with petrelintide 9·0 mg, and 81 with placebo. 255 (53%) participants were female, 230 (47%) were male, mean age was 47 (SD 12) years, mean bodyweight 107·1 kg (20·3), mean BMI 36·7 kg/m2 (5·5), and 419 (86%) were White. Mean percentage change in bodyweight from baseline after 28 weeks (efficacy estimand) was -7·9% (95% CI -9·0 to -6·7) with petrelintide 1·0 mg, -7·9% (-9·0 to -6·7) with petrelintide 2·5 mg, -9·8% (-10·9 to -8·6) with petrelintide 5·0 mg, -9·3% (-10·5 to -8·2) with petrelintide 7·0 mg, and -9·4% (-10·5 to -8·3) with petrelintide 9·0 mg versus -1·7% (-2·8 to -0·5) with placebo. Estimated treatment differences versus placebo were -6·2% (-7·9 to -4·5) with petrelintide 1·0 mg, -6·2% (-7·8 to -4·5) with petrelintide 2·5 mg, -8·1% (-9·7 to -6·5) with petrelintide 5·0 mg, -7·7% (-9·3 to -6·0) with petrelintide 7·0 mg, and -7·7% (-9·4 to -6·1) with petrelintide 9·0 mg. Bodyweight continued to decline to week 42, with reductions of up to -10·7% with petrelintide. The most common adverse event with petrelintide was nausea (79 [20%] of 404 participants vs five [6%] participants with placebo). Vomiting was infrequent with petrelintide (12 [3%] participants vs five [6%] with placebo); active treatment and placebo had similarly low rates for diarrhoea (30 [7%] participants vs six [7%] with placebo) and constipation (28 [7%] vs three [4%] with placebo). No deaths were reported.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Petrelintide achieved clinically meaningful weight reduction and had similar gastrointestinal tolerability to that of placebo apart from predominantly mild nausea during dose escalation, supporting further evaluation as a long-term obesity therapy.

title: Comparative hepatic effectiveness of empagliflozin vs dapagliflozin among individuals with type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: While both empagliflozin and dapagliflozin are known to improve hepatic steatosis and liver enzyme levels, robust phase 3 trial evidence for improving steatohepatitis and fibrosis is currently exclusive to dapagliflozin. Therefore, a head-to-head comparison between two agents is warranted, to compare the hepatic outcomes between empagliflozin and dapagliflozin in individuals with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using nationwide Korean claims data, we constructed a new-user cohort of adults with MASLD, defined as having type 2 diabetes and a fatty liver index (FLI) ≥60, who initiated empagliflozin or dapagliflozin between May 2016 and December 2023. Outcomes of interest were FLI-defined MASLD regression (achieving FLI <30) and decompensated hepatic events (ascites, variceal bleeding, hepatic failure, liver transplantation). After 1:1 propensity score matching, HRs and 95% CIs were estimated using Cox models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 265,098 new users of empagliflozin and dapagliflozin, 101,487 pairs were 1:1 propensity score-matched (mean age 54.3 years; male 71.3%). Compared with dapagliflozin, empagliflozin was associated with a marginally higher likelihood of FLI-defined MASLD regression (HR 1.06; 95% CI 1.00, 1.11). The risk of decompensated hepatic events was comparable (HR 0.99; 95% CI 0.94, 1.03). Dose-stratified analyses yielded consistent findings in both FLI-defined MASLD regression (low-dose: HR 1.19; 95% CI 0.77, 1.83; high-dose: 1.14; 1.01, 1.28) and decompensated hepatic events (low-dose: 0.95; 0.74, 1.23; high-dose: 1.04; 0.93, 1.15).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Among individuals with MASLD, no significant differences were observed between empagliflozin and dapagliflozin in the risk of decompensated hepatic events.

title: Trends in prevalence of type 2 diabetes and intermediate hyperglycaemia in Mauritius from 1987 to 2021 based on results from the oral glucose tolerance test: a repeated cross-sectional study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Data on national trends in the prevalence of type 2 diabetes and intermediate hyperglycaemia using the oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) are scarce. We aimed to identify trends in the prevalence of type 2 diabetes and intermediate hyperglycaemia in Mauritius, a country that has monitored prevalence over 34 years using OGTT.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Non-communicable disease risk factor surveys using standardised protocols were conducted in the general population in 1987, 1992, 1998, 2004, 2009, 2015, and 2021 in Mauritius, with 36 744 survey attendances by adults aged 25-74 years examined. The participation rate was more than 85% in each survey. Participants had fasting plasma glucose measured at the survey site by site staff, and those who were not pregnant or taking glucose-lowering medication had an OGTT. Blood samples were immediately centrifuged to isolate plasma for glucose measurement. Glycaemic status was classified according to WHO 2006 criteria.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: In 1987, the age and sex-standardised prevalence of type 2 diabetes in Mauritius was 14·7% (698 of 5017 people; 95% CI 13·7-15·7), which increased gradually, peaking at 23·3% (1599 of 5833; 22·4-24·3) in 2009, and decreased significantly to 19·9% (899 of 3343; 18·6-21·1) in 2021. This decrease was consistent in direction across sexes, age groups, and ethnicities. The age and sex-standardised prevalence of intermediate hyperglycaemia was 20·8% (1024 of 5017 people; 95% CI 19·6-21·9) in 1987, peaked at 24·9% (1495 of 5833; 23·8-26·1) in 2009, and declined to 15·6% (580 of 3343; 14·3-16·9) in 2021. The proportion of all individuals with type 2 diabetes who were newly diagnosed decreased from 67·0% in 1987 (468 of 698 people) to 32·5% (292 of 899) in 2021.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Mauritius is the first country to show a decreasing prevalence of type 2 diabetes and intermediate hyperglycaemia over time, using the objective, gold standard OGTT-based diagnostic criteria recommended by the WHO. These results underscore that national efforts to prevent and control type 2 diabetes can reduce its burden; systematic monitoring of diabetes and intermediate hyperglycaemia occurrence using the OGTT is crucial.

title: Efficacy of the digital therapeutic glucura combined with CGM in the treatment of type 2 diabetes: a randomised controlled trial over 6 months.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: CGM is increasingly recommended for non-insulin-treated type 2 diabetes according to the ADA Standards of Care 2026. However, its clinical benefit in high-quality standard care remains limited. This study evaluated whether addition of the digital therapeutic glucura, which delivers personalised lifestyle intervention and self-management guidance, improves glycaemic outcomes beyond CGM and standard care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The study was a 6-month, multicentre, open-label RCT conducted at 24 sites in Germany (ID: DRKS00032537). Adults (≥18 years) with non-insulin-treated type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 53-97 mmol/mol [7.0-11.0%], BMI≥25 kg/m2) receiving standard care were randomly assigned (1:1) by centralised stratified block randomisation to glucura or a control app. Participants and study personnel were not masked to group assignment. Both groups used intermittent CGM every 3 months during the study. CGM sensors were not used prior to the study. The primary endpoint was the change in HbA1c from baseline to 6 months. Secondary outcomes included weight change and patient-centric measures.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 327 randomised participants (intervention: n=165; control: n=162), 320 were analysed (ITT population). The standalone CGM control group improved HbA1c levels by 3.3 mmol/mol (0.30 percentage points); however, the intervention group showed greater reductions of 8.7 mmol/mol (0.80 percentage points) with an adjusted difference of -5 mmol/mol (-0.46 percentage points; 95% CI -7, -3 mmol/mol; p=0.00003). Within the intervention group, more participants achieved HbA1c targets (<53 mmol/mol [<7.0%]: 55% vs 31%, OR 3.38, exploratory p=0.0002; <48 mmol/mol [<6.5%]: 27% vs 7%, OR 6.63, exploratory p=0.0001). The mean weight loss was also greater in the intervention group (4.11% vs 1.79%, p<0.0001). Significant improvements in mental health and diabetes-related distress were also observed. The positive effects were consistent across all subgroups. No device-related serious adverse events were observed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: In non-insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, CGM plus standard care yielded less metabolic benefit than CGM combined with glucura. The combination of glucura and CGM also translated into improvements beyond glycaemic management. title: Genetic Susceptibility in Relative Maternal Protection From Type 1 Diabetes.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Type 1 diabetes is half as common in offspring of mothers versus fathers with type 1 diabetes. We investigated whether selective loss of fetuses with high genetic risk during type 1 diabetes pregnancy explains this relative protection.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: In 6,942 live births in The Environmental Determinants of Diabetes in the Young (TEDDY) cohort, we compared genetic susceptibility by family member with type 1 diabetes and tested whether it explained maternal protection from diabetes or its preclinical stages.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The type 1 diabetes Genetic Risk Score 2 extended (GRS2x) did not differ between children with mothers (P = 0.36) or siblings (P = 0.27) versus fathers with type 1 diabetes. Relative maternal protection from type 1 diabetes and islet autoimmunity (IA) was observed with GRS2x adjustment (diabetes: hazard ratio [HR] 0.50, P = 0.01; IA: HR 0.38, P = 0.006) and without adjustment but not during progression from IA to diabetes. This protection waned after age 6 years.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Intrauterine exposure to type 1 diabetes offers relative protection from IA during early childhood and is not explained by genetic susceptibility differences.

title: Blood-Derived DNA Methylation Biomarkers Predict Diabetic Kidney Disease and Map to Epigenomic Remodeling in Renal Cells.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: We undertook this study because albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate often identify diabetic kidney disease risk only after substantial kidney injury in type 1 diabetes. We asked whether blood DNA methylation patterns could predict future DKD progression and improve clinical risk stratification. Genome-wide leukocyte methylation sequencing identified hypomethylated regions and a four-locus methylation risk score (SLC4A4, FSTL4, ICA1, and PTK2) that improved prediction beyond clinical risk models and was validated in 330 participants. Podocyte multiomics showed concordant hyperglycemia-induced hypomethylation and gene activation, supporting the biological plausibility of the blood-derived risk score.

title: Dynorphin A Inhibits Insulin Secretion Through Opioid Receptor-Dependent Modulation of β-Cell Ca2+ Dynamics.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: The role of endogenous opioid signaling within pancreatic islets remains poorly defined. We investigated whether dynorphin A regulates insulin secretion and characterized the receptor requirements for the acute response to applied dynorphin A in mouse and human islets. Applied dynorphin A suppressed glucose-stimulated insulin secretion by remodeling β-cell Ca2+ oscillations through an opioid receptor-dependent, Na+/K+-ATPase-associated pathway. This response required μ-opioid receptors in mouse β-cells and was pharmacologically consistent with δ-opioid receptor involvement in human islets, defining species-dependent receptor mechanisms for the acute response to dynorphin A.

title: Multiple ABCC8 Loss-of-Function Mutations Associated with Paradoxical Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young.
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: The effects of 16 ABCC8 variants, previously reported in heterozygous association with maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY), some with prior diagnosis of hypersinulinism, were assessed in recombinant Kir6.2/SUR1 KATP channels. title: Efficacy and safety of low-dose IL-2 in people with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes (DIABIL-2): a double-blind, multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2b trial.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Type 1 diabetes results from immune-mediated destruction of pancreatic β cells, driven partly by regulatory T-cell (Treg) insufficiency. We previously showed that low-dose interleukin-2 (IL-2) selectively activates Tregs in people with type 1 diabetes. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy of low-dose IL-2 in preserving residual pancreatic β-cell function and select an optimal regimen of administration in this patient population.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This double-blind, multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2b trial was done in 19 academic hospital centres across Belgium, France, Germany, Switzerland, and the Netherlands. Eligible participants were aged 6-35 years; had a diagnosis of type 1 diabetes; received insulin for less than 3 months; and had a peak C-peptide concentration of at least 0·2 pmol/mL. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to a maintenance course of regimen A, regimen B, or placebo (with a 2:1 allocation ratio of IL-2 to placebo within each regimen) and were stratified by pubertal stage (children and adolescents with a Tanner score ≤4 [stratum 1] and adults with a Tanner score of ≥5 [stratum 2]). Both regimens started with an induction course of once per day subcutaneous injections for 5 consecutive days (days 1-5), then a maintenance course of injections (once per 2 weeks [regimen A] or once per week [regimen B]) from day 15 to 351. Adults received 1 million IU per injection, whereas children and adolescents received 0·5 million IU/m2 per injection. The primary endpoint was the change from baseline to month 12 in serum C-peptide area under the curve (AUC) from 0 to 120 min during a mixed meal tolerance test, analysed in the intention-to-treat population. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02411253 (completed).

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Between June 18, 2015, and Nov 19, 2020, 159 people were assessed for eligibility, of whom 18 were ineligible and 141 were enrolled (48 randomly assigned to regimen A, 46 to regimen B, and 47 to placebo). 66 participants were in stratum 1 and 75 in stratum 2. 125 (89%) of 141 participants completed the study and 16 (11%) ended participation early. 54 (38%) participants were female and 87 (62%) were male. For log-transformed C-peptide AUC at month 12, there was no statistically significant difference in the overall population between placebo and IL-2 groups (geometric mean ratio 1·06 [95% CI 0·56 to 2·01]; p=0·85), with similar results when considering each regimen separately and by pubertal status. A marked Treg expansion was observed shortly after treatment initiation, peaking at day 5, with adjusted means of 1·31 (1·24 to 1·37) in the IL-2 group versus 1·04 (0·95 to 1·14) in the placebo group (difference -0·27 [-0·38 to -0·15]). Low-dose IL-2 was well tolerated across all age groups and treatment regimens. Nine (20%) of 46 participants in the placebo group and nine (10%) of 94 in the IL-2 group reported serious adverse events; one in each group was considered probably related to treatment.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Despite robust Treg expansion confirming target engagement, low-dose IL-2 did not preserve β-cell function in people with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes. The inflammatory environment at diagnosis might be too intense for this monotherapy, but the observed safety profile and confirmed biological activity support further investigation of low-dose IL-2 in earlier disease stages or combination strategies.

title: Diabetes and the role of primary care: a global perspective.
type_basis: PubMed文献类型：Journal Article,Review

abstract.text: The global prevalence of diabetes is rising rapidly, with the steepest increases and greatest unmet need occurring in low-income and middle-income countries. Despite strong evidence that early detection and continuous management reduce morbidity and mortality, many health systems face persistent gaps in diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of people with diabetes. Primary care is the most accessible platform for screening and care coordination, and is central to addressing these challenges. Primary care-led models, including nurse-led and pharmacist-led interventions, integrated multidisciplinary teams, and digitally enabled care pathways, have shown improvements in glycaemic control, cardiometabolic outcomes, and health-care use in people with type 2 diabetes across primary care and community settings. Global initiatives, such as the WHO Global Diabetes Compact and UN non-communicable disease targets, emphasise strengthening primary care to deliver equitable, cost-effective diabetes care at scale. Future priorities include workforce development, addressing health inequalities, scalable implementation strategies, and robust evaluation of long-term outcomes to enable person-centred type 2 diabetes care across diverse health-system contexts.

title: Management of Type 2 Diabetes, 2026. A Consensus Report by the American Diabetes Association (ADA) and the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD).
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: The American Diabetes Association and the European Association for the Study of Diabetes convened a panel to update the consensus statement on the management of type 2 diabetes in nonpregnant adults, published since 2006 and last updated in 2022. The target audience is the multidisciplinary health care team providing diabetes care in the U.S. and Europe. A systematic examination of publications since 2022 informed new recommendations. This update has broadened the focus from the management of hyperglycemia to the holistic management of type 2 diabetes and its risk of associated multiple long-term conditions. Fundamental aspects of diabetes care include promoting healthy lifestyle behaviors (healthy eating, 24-h physical behaviors including sleep, and avoiding tobacco and substance use), alongside the provision of psychological support and weight management interventions. For the management of people living with type 2 diabetes, earlier use, potentially from diagnosis, of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and/or glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1)-based therapies to offer organ protection and improve long-term outcomes in type 2 diabetes is advocated. Furthermore, earlier combination use of SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1-based therapies should be considered in people with concomitant cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure. Finally, the ability to transform outcomes for people living with type 2 diabetes is within our grasp through the consistent, equitable, and systematic implementation of strategies and therapies that are already available.

title: Environmental sustainability of offloading care pathways for people with a diabetes-related foot ulcer: a life-cycle assessment.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Insights into the environmental impact of diabetes care are scarce and are absent regarding treatments for diabetes-related foot disease. We aimed to compare the environmental impacts of three offloading pathways for people with a plantar foot ulcer.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a bottom-up, process-based life-cycle assessment according to ISO standards. We defined three evidence-based offloading pathways from first visit to healing: total contact cast (TCC), non-removable walker and removable walker. Inventory data were collected for all activities within scope (materials, waste, transport, energy consumption). Life-cycle assessment was performed using ReCiPe-2016 midpoint and endpoint methods, employing SimaPro and Ecoinvent 3.10. Monte Carlo simulation with 1,000,000 individuals provided the environmental impact per offloading pathway.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Environmental impact was lowest for the removable walker pathway and highest for the TCC for all 18 midpoints and five endpoints. For global warming, the mean impact was 141 kg CO2-equivalents (CO2-eq) (SD: 88; 95% prediction interval 67, 377) for the TCC pathway, 108 kg CO2-eq (SD: 62; 95% prediction interval 59, 276) for the non-removable walker and 90 kg CO2-eq (SD: 57; 95% prediction interval 36, 244) for the removable walker. The largest environmental impact came from patient transport (59-78% of all impact per pathway in CO2-eq).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Diabetes-related plantar foot ulcer treatment pathways with a walker are likely to result in lower environmental impact compared with the TCC pathway, with the lowest impact for the removable walker pathway. This resulted from using a single device (i.e. no replacements required) and, for the removable walker, fewer visits, despite longer time to healing. Taking environmental impact into account may alter clinical decision-making in offloading treatment.

title: Adipocyte-derived exosomal ANGPTL2 promotes beta cell dysfunction via the EIF2α/ATF4/CHOP stress pathway in mice.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Obesity-associated lipotoxicity drives beta cell failure in type 2 diabetes, but the adipose-to-islet signals that promote beta cell dysfunction remain incompletely defined. We hypothesised that angiopoietin-like protein 2 (ANGPTL2) carried by lipotoxic adipocyte-derived exosomes contributes to adipose-to-islet signalling that impairs beta cell function.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Exosomes from palmitate- or PBS-treated 3T3-L1 adipocytes were applied to MIN6 cells and primary mouse islets to assess beta cell function and identity. In vivo, mice underwent adipose-specific Angptl2 knockdown under high-fat diet (HFD) feeding, followed by metabolic phenotyping and assessment of beta cell function. Adipose-derived exosomes from HFD-fed mice with or without adipose Angptl2 knockdown were injected into normal-chow-fed recipient mice, and endocrine marker composition and islet secretory function were evaluated. Mechanistic studies in MIN6 cells used co-immunoprecipitation, pharmacological rescue experiments and Eif2α (also known as Eif2s1) knockdown to interrogate stress signalling.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Exosomes derived from palmitate-treated adipocytes were efficiently internalised by beta cells and resulted in impaired insulin content and secretion, accompanied by reduced beta cell identity markers and induction of dedifferentiation signatures. ANGPTL2 was enriched in lipotoxic adipocyte-derived exosomes and accumulated in beta cells in an exosome-dependent manner. Angptl2 silencing in adipocytes lowered exosomal ANGPTL2 and mitigated islet dysfunction in vitro. In vivo, adipose-specific Angptl2 knockdown reduced islet ANGPTL2 without changing islet Angptl2 mRNA and improved glucose tolerance, with the AUC of the IPGTT decreasing from 2300.2 ± 165.5 to 1583.7 ± 88.8 mmol/l × min (mean ± SD). In adipose-exosome transfer experiments, recipients of HFD-short hairpin (sh)Angptl2-exosome (Exo) showed lower islet ANGPTL2 abundance and improved ex vivo islet glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS), with stimulated insulin secretion increasing from 6.0 ± 0.3% (mean ± SD) in the HFD-sh-negative control (NC)-Exo group to 10.9 ± 0.6% in the HFD-shAngptl2-Exo group. Mechanistically, ANGPTL2 associated with eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2α (EIF2α) and increased protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase (PERK)-associated EIF2α by approximately 2.8-fold, whereas this difference was lost after further normalisation to input EIF2α, supporting a substrate-availability model. PERK inhibition and integrated stress response inhibitor both attenuated ANGPTL2-induced activating transcription factor-4 (ATF4)/C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP) signalling and improved GSIS.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Lipotoxic adipocyte-derived exosomes increase ANGPTL2 abundance in recipient beta cells and contribute to beta cell dysfunction and identity disruption by amplifying PERK-dependent EIF2α/ATF4/CHOP signalling. Adipose ANGPTL2 and circulating exosome-associated ANGPTL2 represent candidate targets and biomarkers for preserving beta cell function in obesity-associated dysglycaemia.

title: BAF60A governs beta cell identity to control systemic glucose homeostasis.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Chromatin remodelling is critical for maintaining pancreatic beta cell identity and function, yet the key regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to investigate the role of the switch/sucrose non-fermentable (SWI/SNF) complex subunit BAF60A in preserving beta cell fate and glucose homeostasis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Pdx1-Cre-mediated BAF60A-knockout (BaBKO) and BAF60A-overexpressing (BaBOE) mice, together with tamoxifen-inducible adult beta cell-specific Smarcd1 knockout (BaBKOTM) and Isl1 knockout (Isl1BKOTM) mice, were generated to evaluate the role of BAF60A in vivo. Glucose homeostasis was assessed through glucose tolerance tests, insulin tolerance tests and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) assays. Multiomic analyses, including RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag) and single-cell RNA-seq, were performed to characterise chromatin accessibility and transcriptional changes. BAF60A-interacting proteins were identified with biotin identification (BioID) and GST pull-down assays. Beta cell lineage tracing was used to assess changes in cell identity. In addition, BAF60A and the dedifferentiation marker ALDH1A3 were examined in pancreatic islets from individuals with and without type 2 diabetes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: BaBKO mice exhibited significant glucose intolerance, impaired GSIS and pronounced loss of beta cell identity, accompanied by the acquisition of non-beta endocrine features. Inducible deletion of Smarcd1 in adult beta cells similarly impaired beta cell maturation and promoted dedifferentiation, as confirmed by lineage tracing. BAF60A deficiency reduced enhancer accessibility and downregulated beta cell identity genes. Mechanistically, BAF60A physically interacts with the transcription factor islet-1 (ISL1) to regulate transcription of target genes. Adult beta cell-specific Isl1 deletion recapitulated key features of BAF60A deficiency and abolished the beneficial effect of BAF60A overexpression on insulin secretion. Conversely, BaBOE mice exhibited improved glucose tolerance and enhanced GSIS under high-fat diet conditions. Adeno-associated virus-mediated BAF60A overexpression markedly reduced beta cell dedifferentiation in BKS-db/db mice. In human type 2 diabetes islets, BAF60A expression was significantly reduced and inversely correlated with ALDH1A3.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: This work establishes BAF60A-ISL1-dependent chromatin remodelling as a key mechanism that preserves beta cell identity and function under metabolic stress, providing mechanistic insight into beta cell failure in type 2 diabetes.

title: Visceral fat endocannabinoid overproduction is associated with insulin resistance and tissue dysfunction in mice and humans.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Visceral adipose tissue (VAT) dysfunction is a major determinant of obesity-related metabolic complications. Circulating endocannabinoids (ECs) correlate positively with visceral fat mass and metabolic risk, suggesting that adipose tissue-derived ECs may contribute to adipocyte dysfunction and systemic metabolic alterations. Although adipocytes possess the enzymatic machinery for EC synthesis, the depot-specific regulation of EC production and the contribution of insulin resistance to EC overproduction in metabolic diseases remain poorly defined.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We quantified the dynamic production of the major ECs 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG) and anandamide (AEA) and related N-acylethanolamines (NAEs) using ex vivo explants of VAT and subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) from obese mice and from individuals with obesity but without type 2 diabetes and those with both obesity and type 2 diabetes compared with their controls. Paired VAT and SAT samples from the same individuals were analysed. Mechanistic regulation of EC production was explored using pharmacological modulation, cannabinoid receptor type 1-deficient mice and cross-species transcriptomic profiling of VAT.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 2-AG was the predominant species produced by human adipose tissue, with VAT exhibiting a 1.9-fold higher intrinsic production than SAT (p<0.001). Obesity alone did not significantly increase EC secretion from either depot. In contrast, VAT explants from individuals with type 2 diabetes showed an increase in EC production (1.7-fold for 2-AG [p<0.05] and 1.8-fold for AEA [p<0.05]) compared with control individuals, whereas SAT remained largely unaffected. AEA production by VAT was positively correlated with chronic glycaemic impairment (ρ=0.4786, p=0.003 for HbA1c; ρ=0.3445, p=0.034 for fasting plasma glucose). Comparative transcriptomic analysis of mouse and human VAT revealed that type 2 diabetes, but not obesity alone, was associated with the repression of insulin-sensitive adipocyte genes, activation of inflammatory and lipid mediator pathways, and upregulation of purinergic receptor expression, consistent with an increased availability of lipid precursors.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Insulin resistance and severe adipocyte metabolic dysregulation, rather than adiposity alone, appear to be the primary determinants of depot-specific EC overproduction. Our findings identify VAT as a major source driving elevated systemic EC levels in type 2 diabetes, highlighting the therapeutic potential of specifically targeting visceral adipose EC signalling to mitigate downstream metabolic complications.

title: Gaps in Diagnosis and Treatment of Patients With Laboratory-Confirmed Diabetes: A National Cohort Study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To characterize gaps in diagnostic coding and pharmacologic treatment among adults with laboratory-confirmed diabetes.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using national commercial and Medicare claims (2017-2023) linked to laboratory results. Adults with laboratory-confirmed diabetes and no prior diabetes/prediabetes were observed for 1 year. Outcomes were type 2 diabetes diagnostic coding and pharmacologic treatment initiation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 27,650 adults with laboratory-confirmed diabetes, 66.6% received both a diagnosis code and pharmacologic treatment within 1 year; 19.7% received a diagnosis only, 4.1% received treatment only, and 9.6% received neither. Compared with HbA1c 6.5-6.9%, higher HbA1c was associated with progressively higher probabilities of diagnostic coding and treatment initiation, whereas greater comorbidity burden was associated with lower probabilities of both outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: One-third of adults with laboratory-confirmed diabetes lacked claims-documented diagnostic coding, treatment, or both, with patterns of care defined by glycemic severity and comorbidity burden.

title: Deuterium metabolic imaging reveals greater liver fat contribution from lipogenesis in South Asian men than European men: a potential mechanism underlying elevated type 2 diabetes risk.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: South Asian individuals are up to six times more likely to develop type 2 diabetes than individuals from other ethnic groups, often at a younger age and lower BMI. It has been shown that liver fat accumulates more readily in South Asian individuals, and this is thought to be a key driving factor contributing to the insulin resistance and diabetes in this population. However, the mechanisms underlying this phenomenon remain unclear. Understanding the role of de novo lipogenesis (DNL) in liver fat accumulation has been hampered by a lack of non-invasive techniques to quantify DNL-derived liver fat. We developed a method to quantify DNL-derived liver fat and used it in a proof-of-concept case-control study, hypothesising that there would be greater liver fat contribution from DNL in South Asian individuals than in European individuals.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A total of seven South Asian and six European participants, matched for age and BMI, underwent deuterium magnetic resonance scans at baseline and after 5 days of 2H water enrichment, from which the fractional and absolute amounts of liver fat from DNL (DNLMR) were calculated. Proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) and MRI were used to determine lipid quantity and composition.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Our method allowed precise quantification of 2H-labelled liver lipids (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC]>0.956), which enabled us to accurately detect changes in liver fat due to DNL. Both fractional and absolute DNLMR were higher in South Asian participants than in European participants (both p=0.041). DNLMR correlated with liver fat content (fractional rs=0.874, absolute rs=0.888; both p=0.001), as well as the saturation ratio of both liver fat (fractional rs=0.692, absolute rs=0.748; both p<0.05) and visceral adipose tissue (fractional rs=0.648, absolute rs=0.708; both p<0.01). Liver fat content correlated with insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) (rs=0.659, p=0.014).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: DNL or related factors may play a pivotal role in driving the increased liver fat and risk of diabetes in South Asian individuals. The novel methodology used to quantify DNL provides a powerful tool for studying DNL-derived liver fat in human metabolic disorders including diabetes.

title: CGM-derived disposition index estimates beta cell function in individuals with islet autoimmunity who do not require insulin treatment; changes in the disposition index precede changes identified by CGM metrics 1 year later.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Monitoring of beta cell function in individuals with islet autoimmunity who do not require insulin treatment (preclinical type 1 diabetes) is normally done via OGTTs, posing major challenges given the invasiveness of the test. Here, we validated a disposition index (DI) derived from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics (DICGM), which is a proxy of beta cell function, against the gold-standard OGTT DI (DIMM), in a cohort of individuals with one or more islet autoantibodies who do not require insulin treatment.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Participants underwent a 3 h 10-point OGTT with measurement of glucose, insulin and C-peptide while wearing a blinded CGM. The sensor was started 24 h prior to the OGTT. DICGM was computed using CGM data during the 3 h OGTT and two blood glucose calibrations, and compared with the DI from the oral minimal model (DIMM), which uses plasma glucose, insulin and C-peptide. The association between the baseline DICGM and duration of glucose levels above 7.8 mmol/l (140 mg/dl) (TA140) at 1 year was explored.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-four participants (median age 16.8 years [IQR 13.5-27.7] ) were enrolled, of whom 18 completed both the OGTT (ten with pre-stage 1, seven with stage 1 and one with stage 3a type 1 diabetes) and CGM at baseline, and had repeat CGM 1 year later. The baseline DICGM was highly correlated with the DIMM (r=0.90, p<0.001). Lower baseline DICGM was associated with higher 1 year TA140 (r=-0.61, p=0.014) and higher 1 year mean sensor glucose (r=-0.62, p=0.020).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Beta cell function can be estimated using CGM during a glucose load. DICGM correlates with a 1 year clinically relevant outcome (TA140) in individuals with islet autoimmunity who do not require insulin therapy.

title: Hashimoto's thyroiditis: two decades on.
type_basis: PubMed文献类型：Journal Article,Review

abstract.text: Hashimoto's thyroiditis is the most common cause of primary hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions and is characterised by immune-mediated injury to thyroid follicular cells. Its pathophysiology involves an interplay of genetic susceptibility, environmental exposures, and epigenetic modifications that disrupt immune tolerance, promoting T-cell mediated thyroid injury and thyroid autoantibody production. The disease can progress from euthyroid autoimmunity to subclinical and overt hypothyroidism, with substantial variation in its course. Clinical manifestations vary with the extent of thyroid dysfunction and inflammatory activity. Diagnosis relies on clinical assessment, thyroid function testing, thyroid autoantibody measurement, and ultrasonography when indicated. Management centres on levothyroxine replacement for overt hypothyroidism, with an individualised approach to subclinical disease. Thyroidectomy is reserved for selected indications, whereas emerging immunomodulatory strategies remain investigational. This Review synthesises developments over the past two decades in the epidemiology, natural history, aetiopathogenesis, diagnosis, and management of Hashimoto's thyroiditis, and considers emerging mechanistic insights and approaches to precision medicine that might inform future disease-modifying therapies.

title: A Multicenter 13-Week Evaluation of the twiist Automated Insulin Delivery in Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes: The twiist-T2D Pivotal Trial.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the efficacy, safety, and user satisfaction of the twiist automated insulin delivery (AID) system in adults with type 2 diabetes.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: In a single-arm, multicenter trial, 307 adults with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, 19-85 years old, initiated use of the twiist AID system for 13 weeks after collection of baseline continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data. The primary outcome was change in HbA1c from baseline to 13 weeks.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean HbA1c decreased by 0.7% (95% CI -0.9 to -0.6) from 8.1% ± 1.5% at baseline to 7.4% ± 0.9% after using twiist for 13 weeks (P < 0.001 for both noninferiority and superiority). The treatment effect was greatest in participants with baseline HbA1c ≥9.0%. A substantial HbA1c reduction was observed when AID was added to prestudy use of a glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist or sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor drug, which was continued during the trial. Mean CGM-measured time-in-range 70-180 mg/dL increased from 57% ± 26% to 73% ± 17% (mean change 16% [95% CI 14-18]; P < 0.001). All other multiplicity-controlled CGM outcomes reflective of hyperglycemia showed significant improvement from baseline. The frequency of CGM-measured hypoglycemia was low at baseline and remained low during follow-up. Diabetic ketoacidosis occurred in one participant; no severe hypoglycemia events occurred. Using twiist, participant satisfaction was higher than with their prestudy insulin delivery method (P < 0.001) and sleep quality improved (P < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this single-arm, 13-week trial in adults with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, AID with the twiist system was safe and associated with substantially improved glycemia.

title: Diabetes Care of Children With Type 1 Diabetes at School: Factors Related to the Choice of Care Location and Association With Glycemic Control.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) management in children requires a comprehensive approach tailored to developmental stages and school environments. This study investigated the locations of self-management behaviors at school, examining factors influencing location choice and their associations with glycemic control.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: This multicenter, cross-sectional study analyzed 2018 registration data from 1,105 children with T1D attending schools or preschools in Japan. Associations among HbA1c, care behaviors, locations, treatment modalities, age, and sex were statistically evaluated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean (SD) HbA1c was 8.01% (1.12%) (64.0 [12.2] mmol/mol). Care locations were the classroom (36.9%), designated rooms (52.6%), and the restroom (5.9%). HbA1c was significantly higher in the restroom group at 8.56% (0.98%) (70.1 [10.7] mmol/mol) than in the classroom group at 8.00% (1.20%) (63.9 [13.1] mmol/mol) and designated room group at 7.95% (1.08%) (63.4 [11.8] mmol/mol) (P < 0.001). Restroom use and omitting prelunch blood glucose monitoring were independently associated with higher HbA1c. Pump use, continuous glucose monitoring, and male sex predicted higher classroom use and lower restroom use. Joinpoint analysis showed that classroom use declined after age 6 (elementary school entry), whereas restroom use emerged from age 11 and spiked markedly at age 16 (20.8%), coinciding with high school entry, even among pump users.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Care location choice shifts dynamically with age and school transitions, with restroom use being linked to poorer glycemic control. Supporting youth during school transitions requires targeted environmental adjustments and enhanced school-wide understanding to ensure safe and appropriate care locations.

title: Olive Oil Before Oral Glucose Delays Gastric Emptying and Lowers Glycemia Through Partially Redundant Glucagon and GLP-1 Signaling in Mice.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: We undertook this study to define how fat consumed before oral glucose attenuates postchallenge glycemia. We asked whether olive oil reduces glycemia by slowing gastric emptying and investigated contributing endocrine and neural pathways. Olive oil increased glucagon, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, and glucagon-like peptide-1; slowed gastric emptying; and reduced early glycemia in mice. Glucagon and glucagon-like peptide-1 signaling acted redundantly, with vagal involvement. Nutrient timing integrates endocrine-neural regulation of gastric emptying and glycemia, supporting evaluation of meal sequencing in humans.

title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring-Guided Insulin Optimization in Patients Receiving Nocturnal Parenteral Nutrition.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate whether a continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system (CGMS)-guided insulin optimization can improve glucose control and nutritional status in insulin-treated patients receiving long-term nocturnal parenteral nutrition (PN).

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective single-center study, 12 insulin-treated adults with chronic intestinal failure undergoing nocturnal cyclic PN underwent 30-day CGM assessment before and after a diabetologist-led optimization of insulin therapy.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Glucose profiles improved after the intervention: less time >250 mg/dL (27% to 17%; -139 ± 113 min/day; P = 0.02), more time in range (44% to 59%; +206 ± 118 min/day; P = 0.002), and without more hypoglycemia. HbA1c decreased by -0.7% (-8 mmol/mol; P = 0.04), and glycosuria resolved in all affected patients (P = 0.03). Body weight increased by +5 kg (interquartile range 4-7.75; P = 0.006), as did serum albumin (+8 g/L; P = 0.006). Malnutrition resolved among 8 of 11 participants (P < 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: CGMS-guided insulin optimization was associated with improvements in glucose control and nutritional status.

type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: Diabetes subtype-specific research is challenging when using data from large registers, and validation studies of Swedish National Diabetes Register (NDR) diagnoses remain limited. We aimed to develop an algorithm to classify diabetes subtypes using linked longitudinal data, compare with NDR, and validate it using polygenic risk scores. We developed an algorithm that reliably distinguishes diabetes subtypes with higher granularity compared with NDR and is validated by polygenic risk scores. Our algorithm reveals clinically meaningful heterogeneity that may be overlooked in registers and enables subtype-specific diabetes research.

title: Genetic background modulates MafAS64F-mediated islet ageing in male mice.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: In monogenic diabetes, there is increasing recognition that common polygenic factors can modulate diabetes penetrance beyond the causative mutation(s). A naturally occurring mutation in the gene encoding the essential islet-enriched transcription factor MafA (MafAS64F) produces an unusually long-lived variant protein that predisposes male carriers to MODY. Here we investigated how genetic background modulates disease penetrance in MafaS64F/+ male mice.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: MafaS64F/+ male mice, either on a mixed genetic background (C57BL/6J and SJL/J) or backcrossed to a C57BL/6J background, were assessed for glucose levels, beta cell function and gene signatures associated with cellular ageing. RNA-seq analysis was performed to identify unique differentially expressed genes (DEGS) and pathways in mixed-background or C57BL/6J MafaS64F/+ male mouse islets. These were overlaid on MafA CUT&RUN peaks to identify direct targets that could differentially impact beta cell function in each background.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: MafaS64F/+ male mice on a mixed background manifested overt diabetes, impaired insulin secretion, accelerated beta cell senescence and dysregulated circadian gene expression, while backcross to C57BL/6J prevented dysglycaemia and maintained insulin secretion in MafaS64F/+ male mice, comparable with control littermates. RNA-seq of C57BL/6J MafaS64F/+ male mouse islets revealed relative normalisation of DEGs associated with cellular ageing and circadian regulation. In addition, islets from C57BL/6J MafaS64F/+ male mice showed unique downregulation of retinoic acid signalling and cell cycle inhibitor p21, the latter of which modulates cellular ageing and diabetes seen in the mixed-background mouse islets. CUT&RUN mapping revealed that MafA directly impacted expression of (at least) retinoic acid receptor-α (encoded by Rara) in islets from C57BL/6J MafaS64F/+ male mice and circadian regulation in islets from mixed-background mice.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: In sum, these data show that genetic modifiers can impact beta cell regulation of retinoic acid signalling and circadian entrainment to modulate beta cell ageing and disease penetrance in mice modelling MAFA-MODY.

abstract.label: DATA AVAILABILITY
abstract.text: Sequencing data were deposited in the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database (accession no. GSE299343 for bulk RNA-seq and GSE298664 for CUT&RUN analyses).

abstract.text: Mitochondrial dysfunction in diabetic kidney disease is compartment and stage specific, reflecting differences in renal cell metabolism, function, and injury response. This article introduces a framework for interpreting mitochondrial dysfunction across renal cell types and disease stages. Proximal tubular stress progresses from increased transport demand to mitochondrial injury and impaired quality control. Distal nephron, immune, and interstitial mitochondrial mechanisms remain incompletely defined. In glomerular endothelial cells and podocytes, mitochondria primarily regulate stress and injury signaling. Cell-specific mitochondrial phenotyping may reveal reversible pathways and guide more precise therapeutic strategies in diabetic kidney disease.

title: Glucose controls metallothionein 1 gene expression in pancreatic islets via a mechanism involving cellular metabolism, granular zinc and the zinc transporter ZnT8 in rat and mouse.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Metallothionein 1 (MT1) negatively regulates insulin secretion in pancreatic beta cells, and is upregulated by low non-stimulating glucose levels compared with physiological glucose stimulation in cultured rodent and human islets. Whether this regulation also occurs in vivo and its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here we examine whether physiological changes in blood glucose levels in vivo control islet Mt1 gene expression similarly to ex vivo observations, and identify the mechanisms involved.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Rats fasted for 1, 2 or 3 days and rats fasted for 2 days and refed for 1 day were compared with rats fed throughout. Mice implanted with subcutaneous insulin mini-osmotic pumps were compared with control mice. Rat and mouse islets were cultured in the presence of optimal glucose levels (10 mmol/l; G10 medium) or low non-stimulating glucose levels (2 or 5 mmol/l; G2 or G5 medium) in the absence or presence of various modulators of mitochondrial metabolism, protein synthesis, Ca2+ influx, autophagy and insulin secretion. Islets from Znt8 (Slc30a8) knockout (KO) mice and corresponding control mice were studied. Gene mRNA levels were assessed by reverse-transcription followed by real-time PCR, plasma and secreted insulin levels were assessed using RIA, intracellular free Zn2+ ([Zn2+]c) was assessed using FluoZin-3, metal regulatory transcription factor 1 (MTF1) activity was assessed using an MTF1-luciferase lentiviral reporter system, and beta cell morphology was assessed by transmission electron microscopy.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among glucose-affected zinc transporters/importers in rat islets, only the zinc efflux transporter Znt1 (Slc30a1) was upregulated under low non-stimulating glucose levels (G2 and G5 medium) vs physiological glucose stimulation (G10 medium), in parallel with Mt1. In vivo, Mt1 mRNA levels were upregulated approximately 3-4-fold in the islets of fasted rats and mice implanted with insulin pumps, with both conditions inducing sustained hypoglycaemia. This effect was fully reversed after normalisation of blood glucose levels. Interestingly, Znt1 mRNA levels changed in parallel with those of Mt1. Hypoglycaemia also markedly altered the expression of beta cell-enriched genes (downregulated), adaptive unfolded protein response (UPR) genes (downregulated), integrated stress response (ISR)/proapoptotic UPR genes (upregulated) and oxidative stress-responsive genes (upregulated). Normalisation of blood glucose levels largely reversed these alterations. In cultured islets, addition to G2 medium of mitochondrial metabolic substrates that bypass glycolysis inhibited Mt1 expression to the same extent as G10 medium. Conversely, the reduction of Mt1 expression in G10 medium was prevented when mitochondrial function or protein synthesis were inhibited. In comparison with fed mice, beta cells of fasted mice had degradative autophagic vacuoles containing secretory granule components. In agreement, islet cells cultured in G2 vs G10 medium showed an increase in [Zn2+]c that was prevented by chloroquine treatment. Co-staining with nuclear and cytosolic markers confirmed the cytosolic and perinuclear subcellular localisation of increased [Zn2+]c in G2 medium. This effect was reproduced in MIN6 cells cultured in G5 vs G25 medium (containing 25 mmol/l glucose, which is the optimal concentration for culture of MIN6 cells) and was paralleled by a significant increase in MTF1 activity, which is a robust indicator of an increase in cytosolic free Zn2+. In Znt8-KO islets, the depletion of zinc from secretory granules prevented the increase in [Zn2+]c and the upregulation of islet Mt1 and other MTF1-regulated genes (Mt2 and Znt1) by low glucose levels.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Physiological changes in glucose levels dynamically regulate islet Mt1 gene expression in vivo as previously shown ex vivo. Mt1 downregulation by glucose depends on active mitochondrial metabolism and protein synthesis, and correlates with reduced [Zn2+]c and MTF1 activity. Its upregulation under low glucose is associated with autophagic degradation of insulin granules, release of intragranular Zn2+ into the cytosol, an increase in [Zn2+]c, and increased MTF1 activity. This upregulation is absent in Znt8-KO islets, thereby demonstrating that it requires a functional ZnT8 transporter. Our findings establish a novel link between MT1 and ZnT8, and shift our understanding of Mt1 regulation from a simple stress-dependent mechanism to a more complex model involving the modulation of cellular metabolism and intracellular zinc dynamics.

title: Contemporary Sex-Specific Mortality Risk in Type 1 Diabetes During the Era of Advanced Therapeutic Care.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Amid major advances in diabetes care technologies, this study aimed to assess all-cause mortality risk among individuals diagnosed with type 1 diabetes in recent decades compared with matched control individuals.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study included all patients with type 1 diabetes diagnosed before age 35 between 2000 and 2022, identified through a validated registry from Maccabi Healthcare Services (MHS), a large state-mandated health care provider network. A diabetes-free comparison cohort was constructed using 1:4 propensity score matching by sex and age. Follow-up continued until 2023, death, or transfer from MHS, whichever occurred first. Cox regression and sensitivity analyses were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mortality rates among 4,299 individuals with type 1 diabetes (mean ± SD age at diagnosis, 17.4 ± 9.1 years) and 17,196 matched control individuals (45.6% female overall) were 131.0 and 35.2 per 100,000 person-years, respectively, with 112 deaths over 204,102 person-years. Type 1 diabetes was associated with higher mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 3.66; 95% CI 2.53-5.31), with consistent estimates after adjustment and sensitivity analyses. Excess mortality was greater in females than males (adjusted HR 8.40 [3.71-19.04] vs. 2.90 [1.78-4.72]; P-interaction = 0.02), although absolute mortality rates were higher in males. Mortality risk was higher in those diagnosed in 2000-2010 than in 2011-2022 (adjusted HR 4.36 [1.22-15.57] vs. 2.94 [1.31-6.60]), with follow-up truncated for comparability.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Type 1 diabetes was associated with higher risk of mortality, particularly among females. This association was attenuated among individuals diagnosed in more recent years.

title: Skeletal Muscle DPT Ameliorates Obesity and Metabolic Dysfunction via the PERK/eIF2α/ATF4-GDF15 Axis.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: We identified dermatopontin (DPT) as a previously unrecognized compensatory regulator that is upregulated in skeletal muscle in obesity and preserves muscle function and systemic metabolic homeostasis, offering a potential therapeutic target for metabolic disorders. Mechanistically, DPT activates an adaptive PERK/eIF2α/ATF4 endoplasmic reticulum stress axis specifically under metabolic stress, but not under normal conditions, which enhances muscle function and directly counteracts metabolic deterioration, revealing a protective signaling cascade. This DPT-driven endoplasmic reticulum stress axis transcriptionally upregulates growth differentiation factor (GDF) 15 expression and secretion in muscle. Muscle-derived GDF15 exerts both local muscle-autonomous and systemic protective effects, uncovering a previously unrecognized muscle-to-organ cross-talk axis.

title: Efficacy and safety of HRS-7535, a novel oral small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, in participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled by metformin and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase II trial.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of HRS-7535, an oral small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA), in Chinese participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately managed by metformin and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase II study included participants aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 58-97 mmol/mol (7.5-11.0%) and BMI 20.0-35.0 kg/m2 and on stable-dose metformin and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor therapy for ≥8 weeks prior to screening. Participants were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive HRS-7535 30 mg, HRS-7535 60 mg or visually matching placebo tablets once daily using a stratified block randomisation method, with treatment assignments concealed until study completion. The primary endpoint was the change in HbA1c from baseline to week 16. Secondary efficacy outcomes included the proportions of participants achieving HbA1c targets of <53 mmol/mol (7.0%) and ≤48 mmol/mol (6.5%), and changes from baseline in fasting body weight to week 16.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 155 participants with a mean baseline HbA1c of 69 mmol/mol (8.5%) were randomly assigned to HRS-7535 30 mg (n=51), HRS-7535 60 mg (n=53) or placebo (n=51). At week 16, the least‑squares mean differences in HbA1c from baseline for the HRS-7535 30 mg, HRS-7535 60 mg and placebo groups were -16 mmol/mol (95% CI -19, -14) (-1.5% [95% CI -1.7, -1.3]), -20 mmol/mol (95% CI -22, -17) (-1.8% [95% CI -2.0, -1.6]) and -4 mmol/mol (95% CI -7, -2) (-0.4% [95% CI -0.6, -0.2]), respectively (p<0.0001 for both HRS-7535 doses vs placebo). The proportions of participants achieving HbA1c <53 mmol/mol (7.0%) were 51.0% in the HRS‑7535 30 mg group, 66.0% in the HRS‑7535 60 mg group, and 9.8% in the placebo group; the corresponding proportions for HbA1c ≤48 mmol/mol (6.5%) were 35.3%, 37.7% and 3.9%, respectively. Body weight loss was -2.4% in the HRS-7535 60 mg group vs -0.7% in the placebo group. Most treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were mild to moderate, and gastrointestinal adverse events were the most common. No severe hypoglycaemia was reported. The only TEAE that led to treatment discontinuation occurred in the placebo group.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Treatment with HRS-7535 resulted in significant improvements in glycaemic management in participants with type 2 diabetes, and the drug exhibited a favourable safety profile. To address a significant clinical data void, this research focused on the addition of HRS‑7535 to the background regimen of metformin and SGLT2i for glycaemic management in participants with type 2 diabetes. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06393348. Funding This study was funded by Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals.

title: Reversal of T1D and Rapid Reduction of β-Cell Stress by IL-10-Dependent MDSCs Induced by TLR4-Ab.
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: Therapy with IgG3 Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/myeloid differentiation factor 2 (MD2) agonistic antibody (TLR4-Ab) is a novel approach to type 1 diabetes (T1D) immunotherapy that targets the innate immune system by inducing immunoregulatory myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs). We sought to define the mechanisms by which TLR4-Ab induces MDSCs and how they reverse T1D. TLR4-Ab induction of MDSCs requires interleukin 10 signaling in the bone marrow, and MDSCs mediate suppression via inducible nitric oxide synthase. Induction of immunoregulatory MDSCs results in profound downregulation of β-cell endoplasmic reticulum stress and unfolded protein response associated with acute T1D. Establishing mechanisms by which TLR4-Ab reverses acute T1D defines new therapeutic pathways for human T1D that target innate immunity to restore immune tolerance.

type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: We determine how innate immunity adapts to transitions between fasting and feeding. Feeding rapidly induced periprandial neutrophilia. HFD accelerated this reponse. We therefore sought to examine whether periprandial states regulate neutrophil dynamics. We identified that the glucagon-like peptide 1 and insulin axis modulates the neutrophil surge, which is critical during endotoxin challenges. The periprandial state prepares the host for endotoxemia. We bridge nutrient intake and incretin-sensitive immunity to inflammatory tone, redefining postprandial inflammation, insulin resistance, and cardiometabolic risk in diabetes.

title: Altered glucagon and GIP responses in South Asian versus Nordic women after gestational diabetes mellitus.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: We aimed to compare ethnic differences in levels of glucagon, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) following a pregnancy complicated by gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and to assess whether the higher insulin levels observed in South Asian compared with Nordic women could be explained by differences in the hormone secretory responses.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We measured glucagon, GIP and GLP-1 in 178 South Asian and 107 Nordic women during an OGTT, and stratified participants by glycaemic status. Glucagon and total GLP-1 and GIP responses when fasting and post-OGTT were assessed by linear mixed models. Ethnic differences in incretin and glucagon levels were evaluated by linear regression analyses. Pre-hepatic insulin levels were estimated using deconvolution of C-peptide kinetics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ethnic differences in glucagon and incretin levels varied by glycaemic status. In the normoglycaemic South Asian group, early (0-15 min) glucagon suppression post-OGTT was significantly attenuated compared with the Nordic group (p=0.002). Fasting glucagon levels did not differ (p=0.139), but total glucagon exposure (including fasting levels) was higher in South Asian women (p=0.013). No differences in GIP and GLP responses to the OGTT were observed (p=0.490 and p=0.802). In women with prediabetes or diabetes, fasting glucagon was higher in the South Asian group (p=0.010), but there were no significant differences in early glucagon suppression post-OGTT (p=0.986). GIP responses to the OGTT were lower among South Asian women (p<0.001), despite higher insulin responses compared with the Nordic women. GLP-1 responses did not differ between the ethnic groups (p=0.661). The higher pre-hepatic insulin levels in South Asian vs Nordic normoglycaemic women were not associated with differences in incretin levels, but were associated with lower insulin sensitivity in the regression analyses (p<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: When examined 1-3 years post-GDM, normoglycaemic South Asian women had less early glucagon suppression and higher total glucagon exposure post-OGTT compared with Nordic women. The higher pre-hepatic insulin levels were not associated with higher incretin levels, but were associated with lower insulin sensitivity.

title: Evolving phenotype of newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes: a 15-year population-based comparison.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Our aim was to describe the phenotype at diagnosis and the early therapeutic profile of newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes across two periods spanning approximately 15 years within the same integrated healthcare system.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study used electronic health record data from Clalit Health Services (Haifa & Western Galilee, Israel). Adults with incident type 2 diabetes in 2005-2008 (period 1: n=80,201) were compared with those diagnosed in 2020-2023 (period 2: n=101,392). Between-period differences are presented as crude estimates, with an age-stratified sensitivity analysis, and quantified using standardised mean differences (SMDs; values ≥0.20 indicate at least a small effect) alongside non-parametric and χ2 tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The median age at diagnosis increased from 63.0 to 66.7 years between the two periods; the proportion aged ≥85 years nearly doubled (from 3.5% to 6.6%). The score for the Charlson comorbidity index increased from 4 to 6 (SMD 0.48); metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) increased from 4.4% to 18.6%. HbA1c at diagnosis decreased from 56 to 53 mmol/mol (7.3% to 7.0%); pre-diagnosis LDL-cholesterol decreased from 2.90 to 2.21 mmol/l (SMD 0.65). Within 31-90 days of diagnosis, use of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors increased from 0.07% to 15.0%, use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) increased from 0% to 11.1%, and sulfonylurea use decreased more than fourfold (20.8% to 4.5%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: The phenotype of newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes has been fundamentally restructured since 2008: patients are older with a higher comorbidity burden but present with better glycaemic and lipid management, with the latter reflecting statin therapy already established before diagnosis. MASLD has emerged as a major but largely ascertainment-driven comorbidity. The shift to SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1RAs alongside declining sulfonylurea use indicates displacement of glucose-centric strategies by a cardiorenal- and weight-driven paradigm. These findings indicate a need for age-appropriate management and trials enrolling very elderly patients.
