title: Prediabetes subtype-based stratification reveals distinct long-term risks for type 2 diabetes.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Prediabetes is heterogeneous, with subtypes defined by impaired fasting glucose (IFG), impaired glucose tolerance (IGT) or HbA1c, each with different risks of progression to type 2 diabetes. We compared progression across these subtypes, and evaluated the benefit of adding insulin secretion and sensitivity to risk stratification.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analysed 7186 Korean adults aged 40-69 years from the community-based Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study, who were followed for up to 20 years with biennial (every 2 years) oral glucose tolerance tests and HbA1c. Prediabetes was classified as IFG, IGT or HbA1c-defined, and further stratified by insulinogenic index (IGI) and insulin sensitivity index (ISI). Cox regression was used to estimate diabetes risk, and multistate Markov models were used to assess annual transition probabilities and time spent in each state.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Compared with normoglycaemia, the adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were 5.84 (95% CI 5.03, 6.79) for IFG, 4.60 (95% CI 4.17, 5.07) for IGT, and 4.68 (95% CI 4.22, 5.19) for HbA1c-defined prediabetes. The risk increased stepwise with the number of criteria met: the aHRs were 3.10 (95% CI 2.81, 3.41) for one criterion, 7.33 (95% CI 6.50, 8.28) for two criteria, and 15.3 (95% CI 12.2, 19.3) for all three. Markov models showed the shortest prediabetes duration (1.7 years) and lowest regression probability (5.4%) in those meeting all three criteria. Low IGI or ISI predicted higher diabetes risk, and dual impairment conferred greatest risk (aHR 4.06; 95% CI 3.37, 4.90). Even normoglycaemic individuals with low IGI or ISI had an elevated risk of diabetes compared to those with high IGI or ISI.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Diabetes progression differs based on both glycaemic subtype and physiological subtype. Integrating IGI and ISI with conventional definitions enhances risk stratification and may help to identify high-risk individuals for earlier targeted intervention.

title: Renal tubule-specific Nrf2 deletion ameliorates diabetic kidney disease by attenuating glomerular hypertension and kidney injury in a mouse model of diabetes.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: We previously reported that expression of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) is upregulated in the renal tubules of humans with diabetes and in mouse models of diabetes. We hypothesised that Nrf2 deletion would ameliorate renal hyperfiltration and kidney injury in Akita mice (a model of type 1 diabetes).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Akita Nrf2RT knockout (KO) mice were generated by cross-breeding tubule-specific (Pax8)-Cre mice with Akita Nrf2 floxed mice on a C57BL/6 background. Male non-diabetic control mice (Nrf2fl/fl), Nrf2RT KO mice, Akita Nrf2fl/fl mice and Akita Nrf2RT KO mice were studied up to the age of 20 weeks (n=8 per group).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The glomerular filtration rate (GFR), kidney hypertrophy, tubular injury score, glomerular basement membrane thickness, podocyte loss and foot process effacement and urinary albumin-creatinine ratio were significantly increased in Akita Nrf2fl/fl mice and were markedly reduced in Akita Nrf2RT KO mice compared with the corresponding control mice. Attenuation of afferent arteriole vasodilation and efferent arteriole vasoconstriction was observed in Akita Nrf2RT KO mice compared with Akita Nrf2fl/fl mice. Furthermore, downregulation of sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) and angiotensinogen expression in renal proximal tubules was observed in Akita Nrf2RT KO mice compared with Akita Nrf2fl/fl mice. Treatment of Akita Nrf2RT KO mice with a selective A1 adenosine receptor inhibitor increased GFR and fractional excretion of glucose, suggesting that enhanced adenosine signalling may contribute to the altered renal haemodynamics through tubuloglomerular feedback and reduced glomerular injury associated with RT-specific Nrf2 deletion.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: These findings suggest that tubular NRF2 plays an important role in the progression of diabetic kidney disease in Akita mice through modulation of the GFR and expression of SGLT2 and angiotensinogen in renal proximal tubules and tubuloglomerular feedback.

title: Amino Acid Profiles Distinguish Glycemic Phenotypes in Childhood and Predict 10-Year Risk of Dysglycemia in Young Adults: The BCAMS Study.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: Prospective evidence linking childhood amino acid (AA) dysregulation with future diabetes risk remains limited. We examined whether AA profiles distinguished childhood glycemic phenotypes and predicted dysglycemia risk in the Beijing Children and Adolescents Metabolic Syndrome (BCAMS) cohort. AA alterations were already detectable in children with normoglycemia and insulin resistance; six AAs were associated with 10-year dysglycemia risk, and their addition to clinical variables improved prediction. Ile showed the largest estimated indirect association with incident dysglycemia through follow-up insulin resistance; dietary Ile restriction in obese mice produced concordant metabolic changes, supporting AA profiling for early risk identification and Ile as a candidate modifiable target.

title: The development of obesity pharmacotherapy: from early challenges and setbacks to recognition by WHO.
type_basis: PubMed文献类型：Journal Article,Review

abstract.text: Obesity is a chronic, progressive disease associated with disability, increased morbidity, and reduced life expectancy. Global prevalence has risen sharply in recent decades, yet obesity and its treatment-particularly pharmacotherapy -have been highly stigmatised. A legacy of early medications withdrawn over safety concerns, together with poor efficacy, and widespread lack of recognition of obesity as a chronic disease contributed to persistent underuse of obesity pharmacotherapy. This underuse changed in the 2020s with GLP-1 receptor agonists and, later, multiagonist therapies, with their substantially greater efficacy, safety, and disease-modifying benefits compared with older agents. Reflecting this paradigm shift, WHO issued global guidelines and included GLP-1 receptor agonists in the Essential Medicines List, albeit for a narrowly defined population. We take a critical historical perspective, charting the highs and lows of obesity medication development and examining the scientific, regulatory, and societal factors that have slowed or impeded the translation of pharmacological advances into safe, effective, and widely accepted treatments for obesity.

title: CCKBR signalling controls human definitive endoderm specification and pancreatic lineage differentiation.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Paracrine signalling by hormone-producing endocrine cells potentially influences pancreatic development, but this feedback regulation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the roles of gastrin (GAST), cholecystokinin (CCK) and their receptor cholecystokinin B receptor (CCKBR) during human pancreatic development.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Human iPSCs were differentiated stepwise into definitive endoderm and then the pancreatic endocrine lineage. To assess CCKBR function, CRISPR/Cas9 was used to generate CCKBR-knockout iPSC lines. We profiled transcriptional states by bulk and single-cell RNA-seq with computational analyses, and complemented these with biochemical assays, flow cytometry (FACS) and confocal microscopy.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: CCKBR expression peaked during definitive endoderm formation and progressively declined during differentiation, remaining detectable in pancreatic progenitors but largely absent from the endocrine lineage. By contrast, GAST and CCK were expressed only transiently during pancreatic progenitor and endocrine lineage formation. Pharmacological activation/inhibition and genetic knockout implicated CCKBR signalling during definitive endoderm formation. Consistently, bulk RNA-seq indicated that CCKBR deletion triggered ectodermal- and mesodermal-associated transcriptional programs and diminished pancreatic lineage specification. During pancreatic induction and lineage formation, sustained CCKBR activation with GAST or CCK attenuated endocrinogenesis and promoted epithelial structure formation. Further analysis revealed the emergence of a pancreatic ductal-like cell formation under prolonged CCKBR stimulation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: This study provides mechanistic evidence that the GAST/CCK-CCKBR axis is functionally important during human endoderm and pancreas development. This pathway is repeatedly required during in vitro pluripotent stem cell differentiation, regulating germ-layer formation as well as ductal vs endocrine fate decisions. These findings support the optimisation of pancreatic differentiation protocols and inform future studies on whether this axis contributes to human pancreas development and disease.

title: Accelerated Epigenetic Ageing in Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Comparison of 10 Epigenetic Clock Measures in Individuals With Type 1 Diabetes.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: We investigated whether an association existed between epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and diabetic kidney disease (DKD) in type 1 diabetes, using 10 clocks and two cohorts, and whether this amplified disease progression. Older EAA phenotypic age and shorter epigenetically predicted telomere lengths were significantly associated with DKD. Progression from normolbuminuria to severely increased albuminuria was associated with increased EAA, and age, epigenetic age, and EAA were significant predictors of progression to end-stage kidney disease. Results support the development of epigenetic biomarkers predicting DKD onset and progression.

title: Clinical Trial Design Considerations for the Development of Disease-Modifying Therapies for Type 1 Diabetes.
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: Several disease-modifying therapies have reduced the progressive loss of β-cell function in type 1 diabetes, with efficacy observed across a wide array of underlying therapeutic mechanisms of action. These successes highlight opportunities to accelerate the development of novel and repurposed type 1 diabetes treatments; however, only one such therapy has received regulatory approval for clinical use and few phase 3 clinical trials have been performed. For bringing emerging therapies to people living with type 1 diabetes as quickly and efficiently as possible, overall regulatory strategy and clinical trial design, especially inclusion criteria and end point selection, are essential, and planning must include their careful consideration. The considerations discussed herein represent a feasible and promising road map for developers of disease-modifying therapies and establish that type 1 diabetes remains a promising area for continued investment.

title: Predictors of Type 2 Diabetes Remission and Relapse After Metabolic-Bariatric Surgery or Medical-Lifestyle Therapy in the ARMMS-T2D Study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Metabolic-bariatric surgery (MBS) is effective in promoting remission of type 2 diabetes, but this outcome is not universally achieved. We identified baseline patient characteristics that predict diabetes remission and subsequent relapse after various MBS procedures versus intensive medical-lifestyle intervention.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: Alliance of Randomized Trials of Medicine vs. Metabolic Surgery in Type 2 Diabetes (ARMMS-T2D) is a 14-year, multicenter study of health outcomes in 262 patients with type 2 diabetes (68% women, age 49.9 ± 8.3 years, BMI 36.4 ± 3.5 kg/m2, HbA1c 8.5 ± 1.5%) previously randomized to MBS (n = 166) or medical-lifestyle management (n = 96). Predictors of remission (defined as HbA1c <6.5% on no glucose-lowering medications) and relapse were determined using univariate time-to-event analyses of prespecified candidate predictors plus agnostic, multivariate least absolute shrinkage and selection operator.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Throughout a median of 11 years (maximum 14 years) of follow-up, 58% of participants randomized to MBS achieved diabetes remission versus 3% with medical-lifestyle management. Predictors of diabetes remission in univariate analyses included shorter diabetes duration, no insulin use, fewer glucose-lowering medication classes used, greater body weight, higher fasting C-peptide and insulin levels, and weight loss at 1 year (all P < 0.05). Diabetes remission predictors in multivariate analyses included baseline diabetes duration, insulin use, and weight change at 1 year (all P < 0.01). Diabetes relapse after initial remission in the MBS group was predicted by longer baseline diabetes duration and greater number of glucose-lowering medication classes used.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Baseline predictors of diabetes remission and subsequent relapse among participants randomized to one of three MBS procedures or a medical-lifestyle intervention should help inform personalized selection of diabetes treatment.

title: Low-Carbohydrate Diets, Nutritional Adequacy, Glycemia, and Perinatal Outcomes in Women With Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Secondary Analysis of the DiGest Trial.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The optimal dietary carbohydrate intake for pregnant women is disputed internationally. Many authorities recommend a minimum of 175 g/day of carbohydrates primarily to support maternal brain glucose requirements and normal fetal brain development. We assessed whether low (<175 g/day) or very low (<120 g/day) carbohydrate intake was associated with altered nutrient intake, glycemia, or pregnancy outcomes in women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: Women recruited to the Dietary Intervention in Gestational Diabetes Trial (DiGest) completed masked continuous glucose monitoring and a 24-h dietary recall at baseline before random assignment to receive either a standard- (2,000 kcal/day) or reduced-energy diet (1,200 kcal/day) from ∼29-36 weeks' gestation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: At baseline, 215 women completed a dietary assessment, of whom 66 (30.7%), 74 (34.4%), and 75 (34.9%) reported standard (≥175 g/day), low (120-175 g/day), and very low carbohydrate intake (<120 g/day), respectively. Women consuming fewer carbohydrates consumed less energy, less dietary fiber, and fewer vitamins (B and E) and minerals but proportionally more protein and fat. Consumption of <120 g/day carbohydrates as assessed at baseline before the intervention was associated with a lower time above range (TAR) >120 mg/dL (-6.8% [95% CI -13.4% to -0.2%]; P = 0.044) and lower birth weight (-9.6 [95% CI -18.7 to -0.6] centiles; P = 0.037), but no difference in large- or small-for-gestational-age birth weight was observed. Low carbohydrate intake as a proportion of total energy intake (<35%) without energy restriction was associated with reduced TAR but not with a difference in birth weight.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Lower carbohydrate intake at baseline was associated with modestly improved glycemia before random assignment in women with GDM, but vigilance to maintain adequate intake of micronutrients and fiber is required.

title: Revisiting the β-Cell: The Key to the Type 2 Diabetes Puzzle: The 2025 Banting Medal for Scientific Achievement Award Lecture.
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: Major discoveries in the past have laid the foundation on which modern diabetes research has been built, and future findings can be anticipated. From this groundwork, we have pursued studies evaluating the role of β-cell function and β-cell mass in the pathogenesis of type 2 diabetes. In considering β-cell function, studies of β-cell responses to intravenous and oral glucose have highlighted the critical nature of interpreting these responses in the face of the prevailing insulin sensitivity, and not as isolated responses. The critical role of β-cell dysfunction in the pathogenesis of prediabetes and diabetes has become apparent. When prediabetes is present, β-cell function is reduced by 40%, while in recent-onset type 2 diabetes it is reduced by >80%. In youth with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes, β-cell function deteriorates at a faster rate than in adults, compatible with their disease being more aggressive. From clinical trials in both age groups, the progression of β-cell dysfunction over time is the basis for deteriorating glycemia, with none of the currently available glucose-lowering agents able to halt this inexorable decline. Reflecting on β-cell mass, this is clearly reduced in people with type 2 diabetes. One basis for this is islet amyloid, which is formed from the normal β-cell secretory peptide islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP) (or amylin). The process of amyloid formation promotes oxidative stress, inflammation, and β-cell death, creating a destructive feed-forward that exacerbates disease progression. Experimental studies demonstrate that reducing amyloid formation reduces oxidative stress, inflammation, and the loss of β-cell mass. Ultimately, preserving β-cell function and mass is critical in striving to prevent and treat type 2 diabetes. Future tactics have to deviate from the current approaches if we are going to be successful in reducing the deleterious effects of a dysfunctional β-cell in type 2 diabetes.

title: A Recipe for Better Diabetes Management: The DASH4D Dietary Pattern.
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: The 2026 American Diabetes Association "Standards of Care in Diabetes" includes extensive nutrition recommendations for people with diabetes but stops short of recommending a specific dietary pattern. Instead, the guidelines recommend that all patients be referred for individualized nutrition therapy. This approach appropriately acknowledges diverse patient needs; however, it is difficult for providers to deliver any form of individualized dietary guidance without a clear starting point to guide them. In this article we examine the tension between the needs for individualization and evidence-based nutritional standards in diabetes care. We argue that the DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) dietary pattern stands out as being supported by decades of evidence from rigorous randomized clinical trials, meta-analyses, and large observational studies that have established its benefit for cardiovascular health. We summarize the recently completed DASH for Diabetes (DASH4D) trial, which demonstrated that a modified version of the original DASH eating plan, adapted for adults with diabetes, significantly reduced blood pressure and improved glycemic control in participants with type 2 diabetes and hypertension. We conclude that while individualized dietary counseling remains the standard of care, the DASH4D diet should be a recommended diet for patients with diabetes.

title: Novel Protein Biomarkers to Monitor Kidney Function Decline and Treatment Response in Individuals With Normoalbuminuria and Type 2 Diabetes.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: Kidney function can decline in individuals with type 2 diabetes despite normal albuminuria, yet current risk stratification relies heavily on urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), which may inadequately capture this process. We investigated whether biomarkers reflecting inflammation, tubular injury, regenerative capacity, and fibrosis improve risk prediction and treatment monitoring beyond UACR in these individuals. title: Protective Effects of PD-L1-Overexpressing MSCs and Their Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Type 1 Diabetes.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: This study was conducted to address the urgent need for novel therapies for type 1 diabetes. We investigated whether programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1)-overexpressing mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (PD-L1-MSCs) and their extracellular vesicles (PEVs) can modulate immune responses and protect pancreatic islets, and whether these effects depend on PD-L1 signaling. title: A prospective controlled study assessing postpartum breastfeeding in women with type 2 diabetes: lower rates associated with elevated BMI rather than diabetes.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Breastfeeding is associated with metabolic benefits for women with type 2 diabetes and their infants, yet breastfeeding rates in these women are poorly described. Obesity is associated with type 2 diabetes and lower breastfeeding rates, making it difficult to disentangle the effects of type 2 diabetes vs obesity on breastfeeding. The primary objective was to examine breastfeeding rates in women with type 2 diabetes compared with normoglycaemic women with either (1) matched BMI or (2) normal BMI. The secondary objective was to examine variables associated with breastfeeding.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Pregnant women with type 2 diabetes (cases) or normoglycaemia (controls) were prospectively recruited. Each case was matched with two controls by age and parity and either (1) matched or (2) normal (18-25 kg/m2) BMI. Data were collected from in-person surveys antenatally, medical records and a 4 month postpartum telephone survey. Analysis included descriptive and inferential statistics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Four months of breastfeeding data were available for 29 women with type 2 diabetes, 29 BMI-matched controls and 28 normal-BMI controls. Breastfeeding rates were similar in women with type 2 diabetes and BMI-matched controls, but both rates were significantly lower than those in normal-BMI controls. 'Full' breastfeeding rates were 24%, 38% and 64% in women with type 2 diabetes, BMI-matched controls and normal-BMI controls, respectively, and were not different between women with type 2 diabetes vs BMI-matched controls (p=0.26) but were lower in women with type 2 diabetes vs normal-BMI controls (p=0.002). 'Any' breastfeeding rates were 55%, 54% and 82% in women with type 2 diabetes, BMI-matched controls and normal-BMI controls, respectively, again showing no difference between women with type 2 diabetes vs BMI-matched controls (p=0.79) but were lower in women with type 2 diabetes vs normal-BMI controls (p=0.03).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Maternal obesity, rather than type 2 diabetes, may be the major determinant of reduced breastfeeding rates 4 months postpartum.

title: Prediabetes and diabetes as drivers of fibrosis in MASLD: roles of obesity, adipose tissue dysfunction and insulin resistance.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Prediabetes and type 2 diabetes have been associated with more severe metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but not all individuals have the same risk and the metabolic drivers remain incompletely understood. To understand why, we examined the roles of obesity, adipose tissue dysfunction and insulin resistance in the development of significant liver fibrosis (fibrosis stage ≥F2) in adults across the glycaemic spectrum.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a prospective, cross-sectional study in a real-world setting of adults attending primary care or endocrinology/diabetes clinics. Transient elastography was used to diagnose steatosis (controlled attenuation parameter ≥274 dB/m) and clinically significant liver fibrosis (vibration-controlled transient elastography liver stiffness measurement ≥8.2 kPa). When ≥F2 was suspected, MR-based imaging or liver biopsy was used to improve stratification. MASLD and significant fibrosis were compared across glycaemic and BMI categories and severity of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR; predominantly hepatic) and adipose tissue insulin resistance (assessed by adipose tissue insulin resistance [Adipo-IR]).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among the 1446 participants, the prevalence of MASLD increased across glycaemic categories from 39% in participants with normoglycaemia, to 55% in those with prediabetes and to 68% in type 2 diabetes. Clinically significant fibrosis also increased across groups, being 1%, 6% and 12%, respectively. In prediabetes, clinically significant fibrosis was rare in lean or overweight individuals even though most had associated cardiometabolic risk factors, but this increased fourfold in individuals with obesity, particularly when associated with severe adipose tissue and systemic insulin resistance. Having obesity and type 2 diabetes had the highest prevalence of clinically significant fibrosis (16%), and again, mostly if associated with insulin resistance. Most participants with clinically significant fibrosis were in the highest quintiles of Adipo-IR or HOMA-IR (Q4-Q5).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: In a real-world cohort from primary care/endocrinology clinics, the prevalence of MASLD increased in a stepwise manner with glycaemic and BMI categories, but the prevalence of fibrosis did not increase in the same stepwise manner and remained rare in the absence of obesity, or in obesity without significant insulin resistance. Prediabetes was a risk factor for significant fibrosis mainly in individuals with obesity and significant insulin resistance. In the context of current guidelines, MASLD risk-stratification may be improved in primary care by establishing the metabolic impact of obesity/diabetes (i.e. assessing insulin resistance by HOMA-IR).

title: Long-term Glycemia and Risk of Death in Cystic Fibrosis-Related Diabetes: A UK Cystic Fibrosis Registry Study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Mortality risk is increased in cystic fibrosis (CF)-related diabetes, but its relationship with long-term glycemia is unclear.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: Using UK Cystic Fibrosis Registry data, we estimated the association between updated interval mean hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and mortality using Poisson regression to estimate mortality rates adjusted for age and sex and rate ratios adjusted for age, calendar year, sex, BMI, pulmonary function, and use of CF transmembrane conductance regulator modulators.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 4,477 individuals contributing 31,311 person-years of follow-up, 758 died. Mortality rates increased progressively with higher updated interval mean HbA1c values. Compared with HbA1c ≤42 mmol/mol, adjusted mortality rate ratios were 1.41 (95% CI 1.15-1.73) for HbA1c >42-53 mmol/mol, 1.66 (95% CI 1.33-2.07) for HbA1c >53-69 mmol/mol, and 1.93 (95% CI 1.53-2.43) for HbA1c >69 mmol/mol.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Higher HbA1c was associated with a clinically and statistically significant increase in mortality among individuals with CF-related diabetes.

title: Metadherin Drives FOXO3a Lactylation and Mitochondrial Dysfunction to Promote Podocyte Injury in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: This study investigated whether metadherin (MTDH) drives podocyte injury in diabetic kidney disease through metabolic reprogramming. We sought to define the molecular mechanisms linking altered glucose metabolism to podocyte mitochondrial dysfunction. We found that MTDH upregulates lactate dehydrogenase A, leading to lactate-driven FOXO3a lactylation that selectively activates proapoptotic genes and disrupts pyruvate kinase M2-mitofusin 2 interaction, impairing mitochondrial fusion. These findings identify MTDH as a central metabolic regulator and suggest that targeting MTDH-mediated pathways, including FOXO3a lactylation and pyruvate kinase M2-mitofusin 2 disruption, may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for diabetic kidney disease.

title: Safety of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors in Older Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cohort Study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) have demonstrated cardiorenal benefits in individuals with type 2 diabetes, but safety data in older adults remain limited. We evaluated the real-world safety of SGLT2is compared with dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) among individuals aged ≥75 years with type 2 diabetes.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a population-based, active-comparator, new-user cohort study using administrative health databases from British Columbia, Canada. We included individuals aged ≥75 years with type 2 diabetes initiating SGLT2is or DPP-4is between 1 January 2021 and 31 December 2023. Primary outcomes were infection, diabetic ketoacidosis, acute kidney injury, fall, fracture, and all-cause hospitalization. Cox regression with propensity score-based standardized mortality ratio weighting was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study included 4,997 SGLT2i initiators (median age, 79 years; 37% women) and 1,289 DPP-4i initiators (median age, 82 years; 50% women). Compared with DPP-4i initiation, SGLT2i initiation was associated with lower risks of acute kidney injury (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.60-0.95) and all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.77-0.98), with no difference in risk of infection. No differences were observed in risk of diabetic ketoacidosis, falls, or fractures, although CIs were compatible with both benefit and harm.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In individuals aged ≥75 years with type 2 diabetes, SGLT2i initiation was not associated with increased risk of harm compared with DPP-4i initiation, although estimates were imprecise for some outcomes. These findings may support consideration of SGLT2is as a treatment option in this population.

title: Target Trial of Semaglutide Versus Dulaglutide or Liraglutide in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the comparative effectiveness of semaglutide versus dulaglutide or liraglutide in patients with diabetes receiving maintenance hemodialysis.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: Using 2011-2022 U.S. Renal Data System and Medicare data, we emulated a target trial evaluating semaglutide versus dulaglutide or liraglutide in patients receiving hemodialysis. Overlap weights were used to adjust for confounders. Fine-Gray models were used to assess death on dialysis and hospitalization. A generalized estimating equation was used for repeated measures of body weight.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We identified 1,312 semaglutide and 2,601 dulaglutide or liraglutide users. After overlap weighting, the effective sample size was 3,200 patients (mean age 61; 63% White; 28% Black; 52% male; median [interquartile range] BMI 34 [29-40] kg/m2; median follow-up 1.1 [0.6-1.9] years). Semaglutide versus dulaglutide or liraglutide was associated with a mortality on dialysis subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) of 0.82 (95% CI 0.70-0.97; 1-year cumulative incidence 11% vs. 13%) and all-cause hospitalization sHR of 0.91 (95% CI 0.83-0.99; 1-year incidence 57% vs. 62%). Body weight loss was higher with semaglutide (-4.8%, 95% CI -5.3% to -4.2%) at 1 year vs. -3.4%, 95% CI -3.9% to -3.1%). Direct comparisons of semaglutide versus dulaglutide showed similar results for mortality (sHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.69-0.97) and hospitalization (sHR 0.88, 95% CI 0.81-0.97), but semaglutide versus liraglutide showed no statistically significant benefit for mortality or hospitalization.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among patients with diabetes receiving hemodialysis and equipoise between semaglutide and dulaglutide or liraglutide, semaglutide may be the preferred glucagon-like peptide 1 agent compared with dulaglutide.

title: A Phase 2, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Acmopatide (CT-868), a Fully Biased GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist, in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes and Overweight or Obesity.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acmopatide, a signal-biased glucagon-like peptide 1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonist, in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and overweight/obesity.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: In this phase 2, 16-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study, adults with T1D (HbA1c 7.0-10.0%; BMI ≥27 kg/m2) were randomized 1:1:1:1 to once-daily subcutaneous acmopatide (1.8, 4.1, or 6.6 mg) or volume-matched placebo. The primary end point was change from baseline (CFB) in HbA1c (%) at week 16; secondary end points included percent CFB in body weight and insulin dose.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 111 participants were randomized (placebo n = 29, acmopatide 1.8 mg n = 27, 4.1 mg n = 28, 6.6 mg n = 27). Mean (SD) baseline HbA1c was 7.5% (0.6), and mean BMI was 34.3 (5.6) kg/m2. Acmopatide improved HbA1c (least squares [LS] mean CFB -0.4 to -0.6% vs. -0.3% with placebo; nominally significant placebo-adjusted difference for 4.1 mg: -0.3% [90% CI -0.6 to -0.1]; P = 0.020). HbA1c <7.0% was achieved by 55.6% of participants receiving acmopatide 4.1 mg vs. 33.3% receiving placebo. Acmopatide-treated participants demonstrated reductions in body weight (LS mean CFB -3.3 to -6.7% vs. 0.3% with placebo; all P < 0.01), total daily insulin dose (-3.4 to -14.9% more than placebo for acmopatide 4.1 and 6.6 mg), and mean systolic blood pressure (-3.1 to -8.4 mmHg vs. -3.3 mmHg with placebo). Adverse events were primarily gastrointestinal. No diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or severe hypoglycemia events occurred.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In adults with T1D and overweight/obesity, acmopatide was associated with improved glycemic control and clinically meaningful weight loss without DKA or severe hypoglycemia events.

title: Gene-by-Sleep Duration Interaction for Glycemic Traits in More Than 480,000 Individuals.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: The biological mechanisms of how sleep duration impacts type 2 diabetes pathogenesis and glycemic control are unclear. This study reveals 16 loci (11 novel) that interact with either short or long sleep duration to influence hemoglobin A1c, fasting glucose, or fasting insulin. Short and long sleep duration loci were nonoverlapping. Regulation of copper and diacylglycerol levels appear as distinct cellular mechanisms implicated by long and short sleep duration loci, respectively. Identified gene targets present insight for potential type 2 diabetes therapeutic design approaches related to JIP1-c-Jun N-terminal kinase interaction disruption, pericyte health, N-methyl-d-aspartate receptor activity, anti-inflammatory and leptin-enhancing dietary supplements, and serpins.

title: Reactions to Race[ism]: The Relationship Between Differential Treatment Based on Race and Diagnosed Diabetes Status in U.S. Adults.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine associations between diabetes status and self-reported discrimination based on race among U.S. adults with and without diabetes.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed 2022-2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data from 328,056 adults completing the Reactions to Race module and reporting diabetes status. Experiences of racial discrimination at work, in health care, or elsewhere, and related physical symptoms, were categorized as any versus none. Weighted prevalence and multivariable logistic regression were stratified by diabetes status.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Discrimination based on race was reported by 14.2% of adults with diabetes and 12.5% without diabetes. Patterns were similar across age, metropolitan status, and employment subgroups. In both groups, discrimination was associated with race and ethnicity, age, sex, employment, poor mental health, and current smoking.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Experiences of racial discrimination were common among U.S. adults and were reported more frequently by adults with diabetes. Because discrimination can contribute to chronic stress, reduced access to high-quality care, and barriers to diabetes self-management, consideration of racism-related exposures is important in efforts to understand and address diabetes disparities.

title: CYP1B1: A Context-Dependent Regulator of Metabolism in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: This study systematically dissects the regulatory role of CYP1B1 in the pathogenesis of diabetic kidney disease (DKD). CYP1B1 participates in the progression of DKD by mediating the metabolism of arachidonic acid, retinoic acid, and estradiol, as well as the process of ferroptosis. Its 4-OHE2 quinone metabolites and proferroptotic effect promote renal injury, while it is associated with the maintenance of renoprotective signaling. The net effect of CYP1B1 is regulated by substrate type, cell type, and disease stage, and it can serve as an epigenetic marker and gut-kidney axis mediator in DKD.

title: Extracellular vesicles from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells protect grafted islets against endoplasmic reticulum stress-induced mitochondrial dysfunction via modulating XBP1-based calcium homeostasis.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Although islet transplantation is an ideal option for individuals with diabetes, early graft failure due to beta cell apoptosis and stress-induced dysfunction severely limits long-term efficacy. Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hucMSCs) have multiple functions including maintaining cellular homeostasis. However, it remains unknown as to whether extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from hucMSCs (hucMSC-EVs) provide protective effects against transplant-related trauma-induced islet injury. This study aimed to investigate the effects of hucMSC-EVs on islet graft survival in a syngeneic mouse model of islet transplantation and to examine the mechanism of protection.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: EVs were isolated from cultured hucMSCs and characterised by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking and western blotting. The effects of hucMSC-EVs on islet graft function were evaluated in a mouse model of streptozocin-induced diabetes via co-transplantation under the kidney capsule. Beta cell survival and function were assessed by immunofluorescence, TUNEL staining, insulin secretion assays and in vivo imaging. Endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) and mitochondrial dysfunction were further analysed in primary islets and NIT-1 beta cells under thapsigargin- or tunicamycin-stimulated ERS models. Further calcium imaging, JC-1 staining, western blotting and Seahorse assays were performed. microRNA sequencing was conducted and the role of miR-182-5p and XBP1 in mediating hucMSC-EV function was verified using knockdown, overexpression and dual-luciferase assays.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Co-transplantation of hucMSC-EVs with 250 islet equivalents significantly improved glycaemic control (p<0.01) and glucose tolerance (p<0.01) in diabetic mice. Apoptotic beta cells were significantly reduced in grafts receiving EVs, as shown by TUNEL assays (p<0.05) and cleaved caspase 3 staining (p<0.05). Ex vivo, hucMSC-EVs were internalised by beta cells and protected against tunicamycin-induced apoptosis (p<0.01), preserved insulin expression and restored glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. While ERS enhanced interactions between endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria, hucMSC-EVs maintained calcium homeostasis, improved mitochondrial energy metabolism and alleviated ERS. Small RNA sequencing and functional analysis identified that XBP1-targeted miR-182-5p was enriched in hucMSC-EVs, which further fine-tuned endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria communication via reducing inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate receptors at mitochondria-associated membranes and activated Nrf2 to restore mitochondrial calcium homeostasis under ERS. miR-182-5p inhibition reversed the protective effects of EVs on beta cell calcium homeostasis and viability. In vivo, depletion of miR-182-5p in hucMSC-EVs abolished the ability to prevent beta cell apoptosis and improve glycaemic control in diabetic mice.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: hucMSC-EVs significantly improved the survival and function of islet grafts by delivering miR-182-5p, which targeted XBP1 to modulate mitochondria-associated membranes, attenuate ERS and restore mitochondrial calcium homeostasis. These findings highlight a novel cell-free EV-based therapeutic strategy for improving the outcome of islet transplantation.

title: Clinical and metabolic subtypes of recent-onset adult type 1 diabetes: a prospective cohort study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Adult-onset type 1 diabetes exhibits substantial heterogeneity. We aimed to investigate whether this variability reflects distinct disease entities or different temporal stages of a shared autoimmune process.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective cohort study, we analysed data from adults (aged 18-69 years) in the German Diabetes Study who had clinically diagnosed type 1 diabetes within the preceding 12 months, and from individuals who were positive for glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody (GADA) but had originally been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. We used unsupervised machine learning based on GADA status, fasting C-peptide, glucose, triglycerides, and HDL cholesterol to characterise clinical and metabolic type 1 diabetes subtypes. The resulting subtypes were compared for aetiological traits (polygenic risk scores for type 1 diabetes and type 2 diabetes, partitioned type 2 diabetes polygenic risk scores, human leukocyte antigen [HLA] profiles, and islet-directed autoantibodies), insulin sensitivity, glucagon-stimulated C-peptide trajectories as a measure of residual β-cell function, and complications during prospective follow-up. Reproducibility was assessed in adults with type 1 diabetes from the German Diabetes Prospective Follow-up Registry (Diabetes-Patienten-Verlaufsdokumentation [DPV]).

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Analysed participants in the German Diabetes Study cohort were recruited between June 27, 2005, and Jan 20, 2025 (n=600), and were followed up for a mean of 6·1 (SD 4·7) years. We identified three type 1 diabetes subtypes: two GADA-positive subtypes, and one GADA-negative subtype. A similar clinical and metabolic subtype structure was observed in the DPV cohort, whose participants were recruited between 2000 and 2025 (n=483) and were followed up for a mean of 3·1 (SD 5·0) years. One GADA-positive subtype was characterised by lower BMI, higher insulin sensitivity, and severe β-cell dysfunction (classic type 1 diabetes), whereas the second showed higher BMI, lower insulin sensitivity, and better β-cell function (mixed type 1 diabetes). The two GADA-positive subtypes did not differ in autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes polygenic risk scores, whereas the GADA-negative subtype had lower genetic type 1 diabetes risk, despite no clear subtype-specific differences in HLA risk haplotypes. Longitudinal modelling indicated that the mixed type 1 diabetes group was positioned 6·1 years (95% CI 4·6-7·8) earlier along the β-cell function decline trajectory compared with the classic type 1 diabetes group. The risks of hypoglycaemia (log-rank p=0·0019), retinopathy (mixed type 1 diabetes vs classic type 1 diabetes: adjusted hazard ratio 4·93 [95% CI 1·71-14·24]), and cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (log-rank p=0·028) differed across the groups.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Our results indicate that individuals with combined autoimmunity and lower insulin sensitivity present with clinical diabetes earlier than classic type 1 diabetes along the β-cell decline trajectory, identifying a potential timeframe for disease-modifying interventions in specific type 1 diabetes subtypes.

title: Efficacy and safety of oral orforglipron in Japanese participants with obesity disease (ATTAIN-J): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Orforglipron, a small-molecule, non-peptide, oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, has shown bodyweight reduction and cardiometabolic benefits in adults with obesity across phase 3 trials globally. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of orforglipron versus placebo for treating obesity disease in Japanese adults.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: ATTAIN-J was a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial conducted across 16 medical research centres and hospitals in Japan and included adults aged 18 years or older with a BMI between 27 kg/m2 and less than 35 kg/m2 and two or more obesity-related health disorders, or a BMI of 35 kg/m2 or higher and one or more obesity-related health disorder, with one or more of the obesity-related health disorders being hypertension, dyslipidaemia, or type 2 diabetes (targeted at about 25% of participants), consistent with Japanese indications for tirzepatide and semaglutide for obesity disease; and at least one unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose weight. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) via a computer-generated sequence to once-daily oral orforglipron (6 mg, 12 mg, or 36 mg) or placebo. Co-primary endpoints were mean percentage change in bodyweight and percentage of participants with at least 5% bodyweight reduction from baseline to week 72. Efficacy endpoints were primarily evaluated by the treatment regimen estimand in all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed in participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05931380 (completed).

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Between July 31, 2023, and June 19, 2025, 291 participants were screened, of whom 238 (144 [61%] males and 94 [39%] females; mean age 54·1 years [SD 11·2]) were randomly assigned to receive orforglipron 6 mg (n=61), 12 mg (n=57), or 36 mg (n=60), or placebo (n=60); 214 (90%) participants completed the study. At week 72, mean percentage change in bodyweight was -5·9% (95% CI -7·6 to -4·2) with orforglipron 6 mg, -8·7% (-10·9 to -6·5) with 12 mg, and -7·9% (-10·0 to -5·8) with 36 mg, compared with -0·6% (-2·1 to 0·8) with placebo (all p<0·0001 vs placebo). At week 72, a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% was seen in 15·2% (SE 4·8; nine of 60) of participants in the placebo group compared with 45·6% (6·1; 28 of 61; p=0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 6 mg group, 60·8% (6·4; 35 of 57; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 12 mg group, and 58·8% (6·5; 35 of 60; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 36 mg group. Adverse events with orforglipron were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal symptoms. Across all orforglipron groups, treatment-emergent adverse events that most frequently led to study treatment discontinuation were nausea (one [2%] of 61 in the 6 mg group, one [2%] of 57 in the 12 mg group, and five [8%] of 60 in the 36 mg group vs none with placebo) and vomiting (none in the 6 mg group, two [4%] in the 12 mg group, and one [2%] in the 36 mg group vs none in the placebo group).

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: In Japanese adults with obesity disease, once-daily orforglipron resulted in statistically superior reductions in bodyweight versus placebo, with a safety profile consistent with that of other GLP-1 receptor agonists.

title: Longitudinal Changes in Exocrine Biomarkers in Children at Risk of Type 1 Diabetes in the ENDIA Study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The exocrine pancreas is increasingly implicated in type 1 diabetes. Noninvasive biomarkers of exocrine function, fecal elastase-1 (FE-1) and serum immunoreactive trypsin (IRT), may provide early insight into disease pathogenesis. We investigated the temporal relationship between exocrine biomarkers and type 1 diabetes development in children.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: FE-1 and IRT concentrations were measured prospectively in 301 at-risk children followed in the Environmental Determinants of Islet Autoimmunity (ENDIA) cohort from birth. A total of 216 children provided 1,679 stool samples; 242 provided 1,014 serum samples. Biomarker trajectories were compared between children who developed islet autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes and age- and sex-matched control children negative for autoantibodies in a nested case-control design. Adjusted linear mixed models were used.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Two biomarker patterns were observed. FE-1 concentrations were lower during the first 6 months of life in children who subsequently developed multiple islet autoantibodies or type 1 diabetes (β-coefficient at birth -0.61 [95% CI -1.04, -0.17]; P = 0.006; β-coefficient at 3 months -0.39 [95% CI -0.69, -0.09]; P = 0.010); IRT concentrations were lower in children who developed type 1 diabetes 12 months (β = -0.30 [95% CI -0.58, -0.02]; P = 0.034) and 18 months (β = -0.40 [95% CI -0.71, -0.10]; P = 0.008) before type 1 diabetes diagnosis.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Changes in exocrine biomarkers were detectable early in the natural history of type 1 diabetes, with a delayed rise of FE-1 in infants who later progressed to multiple islet autoantibodies or type 1 diabetes and a decrease in IRT following islet autoantibody seroconversion.

title: Gout as a risk factor for lower-extremity amputation in diabetes: a nationwide, register-based case-control study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Non-healing diabetic foot ulcers are a major precursor to lower-extremity amputation (LEA) in diabetes, and gout may be an overlooked contributor. We hypothesised that individuals with both diabetes and gout have a higher risk of LEA than those with diabetes alone, with the strongest effect at more distal amputation levels.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In a nationwide case-control study of 601,541 individuals with type 2 diabetes, we identified 4912 cases with LEA and 39,101 age- and sex-matched control participants. Gout exposure was determined using ICD-10 diagnoses and Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical codes for urate-lowering therapy. Associations were estimated using conditional logistic regression, adjusting for diabetes duration, peripheral arterial disease, acute myocardial infarction and late diabetes complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Gout was associated with an increased risk of LEA (OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.69, 2.02) in unadjusted analyses, and the association remained significant after full adjustment (OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.37, 1.69). A significant trend (p=0.03) was observed across amputation levels, with potentially higher risk at more anatomically distal sites although no statistically significant differences were observed between individual amputation levels: OR 1.37 (95% CI 1.12, 1.68) for above-knee amputations, increasing to OR 1.65 (95% CI 1.32, 2.05) for toe amputations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Co-existing gout is an independent risk factor for LEA in individuals with type 2 diabetes. The risk is elevated across all amputation levels, with the most pronounced effect potentially being at distal anatomical sites. These findings highlight the need for increased awareness of gout when managing individuals with type 2 diabetes at risk of LEA.

title: Presentation, management, and outcomes of ectopic Cushing syndrome: an international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Ectopic Cushing syndrome is a rare condition with scarce outcome data. We sought to characterise its course and determinants of complications and mortality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study, 49 high-volume endocrine referral centres across Asia, Europe, North America, South America, and New Zealand identified consecutive eligible patients. We included patients with a clinical diagnosis of ectopic Cushing syndrome, defined by expert adjudication at the treating institution with at least one of the following criteria: inferior petrosal sinus sampling or dynamic testing supportive of ectopic Cushing syndrome, biochemical remission of hypercortisolism following treatment of the ectopic Cushing syndrome source (surgical excision, radiotherapy, or cryoablation), evidence of a non-metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome, either on initial or subsequent imaging, or evidence of a metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome either on imaging or from chart notes. Data collection was completed between May 31, 2024 and April 22, 2025. Clinical features, biochemical severity, management, complications, and mortality were assessed. The primary outcome was Cushing syndrome-related mortality (investigator-adjudicated). Secondary outcomes were overall mortality and incidence of complications. Outcomes were stratified based on biochemical remission and timeline since diagnosis. Early (within 6 months of diagnosis) and late (>6 months after diagnosis) outcomes were analysed using landmark methods.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Among 1463 patients (median age 51 years [IQR 37-64; range 3-87], 824 [56·3%] women, 639 [43·7%] men, and 1021 [69·8%] of White race), 836 (57·1%) had metastatic disease. Severe hypercortisolism (1204 [91·1%] of 1321) and hypokalaemia (1111 [79·4%] of 1399) were common. Median duration of follow-up was 57 months (IQR 19-124). Cushing syndrome-related death occurred in 196 (13·4%) patients. 626 (42·8%) patients died overall. Infection occurred in 464 (31·7%) patients, venous thromboembolism in 124 (8·5%), cardiovascular events in 93 (6·4%), and cerebrovascular events in 37 (2·5%). Achievement of complete biochemical remission within 6 months of diagnosis was independently associated with lower risk of late complications (adjusted HR 0·55 [95% CI 0·38-0·80]) and Cushing syndrome-related mortality (0·49 [0·27-0·89]), whereas no association was observed with non-Cushing syndrome-related mortality.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Outcomes in ectopic Cushing syndrome are driven by early control of hypercortisolism. Failure to achieve remission within 6 months is associated with markedly worse complications and mortality, supporting ectopic Cushing syndrome as a time-critical endocrine emergency.

title: Genetic subtyping of MASLD reveals a glucose-lowering axis linked to GCKR alternative splicing.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a global metabolic condition with a complex relationship to type 2 diabetes. Yet human genetic studies suggest the existence of a MASLD subtype with favourable glycaemic effects, raising a clinically important question: how can hepatic steatosis coexist with improved glycaemic outcomes? We aimed to determine whether MASLD comprises genetically distinct subtypes with divergent glycaemic consequences, and to define the genetic basis of a glucose-lowering MASLD subtype.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We integrated genetic and triglyceride-related metabolomic profiles to cluster 18 established MASLD-associated variants and construct mutually adjusted partitioned polygenic risk scores (PRSs) in the UK Biobank. We tested associations with hepatic biomarkers, liver outcomes and type 2 diabetes, and replicated glycaemic findings in an independent Chinese cohort (the Taizhou Longitudinal Study [TZL]). We prioritised candidate loci using colocalisation and fine-mapping and performed allele-specific functional assays and structural modelling to investigate the underlying mechanism at the lead locus.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Partitioned PRSs revealed bidirectional glycaemic axes: one PRS lowered fasting glucose and type 2 diabetes risk, whereas the remaining PRSs increased both, despite all associating with higher liver injury markers and adverse liver outcomes. The divergent glycaemic effects were replicated in the TZL. To pinpoint the genetic basis of the glucose-lowering axis, colocalisation and fine-mapping prioritised GCKR rs1260326 (C>T) as a shared MASLD-type 2 diabetes signal and the lead cis-pQTL for circulating glucokinase regulatory protein (GKRP). Functional experiments showed that the rs1260326 T allele promotes exon-15 skipping in GCKR, reduces the abundance of full-length GKRP and yields a truncated protein. In silico structural modelling suggested that the truncated GKRP isoform may have reduced binding affinity for glucokinase, although this predicted effect requires experimental validation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: MASLD comprises genetically distinct subtypes with opposing glycaemic and type 2 diabetes risk profiles. Within the glucose-lowering subtype, rs1260326-mediated alternative splicing of GCKR provides a potential mechanistic link to reduced GKRP abundance and glycaemic protection. These findings support a more granular view of MASLD heterogeneity and may inform future subtype-specific risk stratification and prevention.

title: Common Genetic Variants Near SLC2A2 and Glycemic Response to Glimepiride in the GRADE Comparative Effectiveness Clinical Trial.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Optimizing second-line therapy for type 2 diabetes remains challenging because of interindividual variability in response. Current treatment selection does not consider personal genetic profiles. To address this gap, we conducted a pharmacogenomic genome-wide association study (GWAS) in a randomized comparative effectiveness trial to identify genetic predictors of glycemic response to insulin glargine, glimepiride, liraglutide, and sitagliptin when added to metformin.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: In the Glycemia Reduction Approaches in Type 2 Diabetes: A Comparative Effectiveness Study (GRADE), we performed a GWAS for the time to reach primary (glycated hemoglobin [HbA1c] ≥7%) and secondary (HbA1c >7.5%) metabolic failure. We conducted replication in independent cohorts, performed fine mapping of the top variants near SLC2A2, evaluated them for physiologic impact using oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT) and response to acute glipizide challenge, and characterized glycemic response to glimepiride in an slc2a2-mutated zebrafish model.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: rs2129019 in SLC2A2 encoding GLUT2 was enriched in African/African American participants and conferred a 38% increased risk of metabolic failure per A allele on glimepiride (P = 1.55 × 10-8). Carriers had impaired β-cell function, evidenced by a lower C-peptide index during OGTT, and diminished glucose-lowering response to acute sulfonylurea challenge. Genetic manipulation in zebrafish confirmed that slc2a2 disruption attenuated the glucose-lowering effect of glimepiride.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Genetic variation influences glycemic response to glucose-lowering medications, with SLC2A2 emerging as a genetic factor that modulates sulfonylurea response. These findings warrant further study to evaluate whether low-response allele carriers would benefit from alternative glucose-lowering therapies to advance precision diabetes care.

title: Real-world evidence for decisions in diabetes.
type_basis: PubMed文献类型：Journal Article,Review

abstract.text: Randomised controlled trials underpin the evidence base for diabetes interventions but have important limitations, including being conducted in selective populations, with restricted follow-up times and treatment pathways that differ from routine clinical practice. Real-world data (RWD) offer an opportunity to address questions beyond the scope of trials, including the comparative effectiveness of interventions, assessment of longer-term outcomes, and treatment effects in under-represented populations. However, the credibility of real-world evidence (RWE) varies widely due to data quality and methodological challenges. The REDDIE (Real-world Evidence for Decisions in Diabetes) programme examined how RWD can generate robust, decision-relevant evidence for diabetes by analysing multiple national registries, evaluating regulatory expectations and conducting target trial emulations of landmark studies. Evidence from REDDIE and the wider literature demonstrates that well-designed observational analyses can replicate major trial findings and extend evidence to broader populations. However, credibility critically depends on careful alignment between the research question, database fitness, study design and analytical methods. Target trial emulation and modern causal inference approaches can mitigate key biases but cannot overcome fundamental limitations of routine data, including unmeasured confounding and incomplete variable capture. RWE and RCTs should be viewed as complementary sources of evidence. We outline a practical framework for the design, analysis and interpretation of RWE studies in diabetes to support more robust and decision-relevant use of RWD by regulators, health technology assessment agencies and clinicians.

title: Associations of long-term exposure to air pollution with glucose homeostasis biomarkers and diabetes-related comorbidities in people with recent-onset type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Air pollution (AP) contributes to diabetes progression and comorbidities, but underlying mechanisms remain unclear, as no observational studies have applied gold-standard phenotyping or distinguished between the effects of type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes and diabetes subtypes. We examined whether AP exposure was associated with glucose homeostasis biomarkers and diabetes-related comorbidities in people with recent-onset type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes and diabetes subtypes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional analysis is based on data from 1120 participants in the German Diabetes Study (417 with type 1 diabetes and 703 with type 2 diabetes). The glucose homeostasis biomarkers used were HbA1c, insulin sensitivity (clamp-derived M value), insulin secretion (glucagon-stimulated C-peptide6min) and insulin clearance (clamp derived). Diabetes-related comorbidities included CVD risk (SCORE2-Diabetes), V ˙ O 2 max as an indicator of cardiorespiratory fitness, albuminuria as a marker of kidney function and the presence of distal sensorimotor polyneuropathy (DSPN). Five-year means of exposure to AP (particulate matter [PM] with diameters of <2.5 μm [PM2.5] and <10 μm [PM10] and nitrogen dioxide [NO2] before baseline at individual residential addresses were examined. Associations between each exposure-outcome pair were estimated per 1 IQR increase in air pollutants using multivariable linear and logistic regression. Two-pollutant analysis, cumulative risk index (CRI) analysis and insulin-treated type 1 diabetes model analysis were performed as sensitivity analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among those with type 1 diabetes, higher PM2.5 was associated with higher HbA1c (exp[β]=1.07 [95% CI 1.03, 1.11]), insulin secretion (exp[β]=1.19 [95% CI 1.03, 1.36]), lower V ˙ O 2 max (exp[β]=0.94 [95% CI 0.89, 0.99]) and higher albuminuria (exp[β]=1.72 [95% CI 1.34, 2.20]). Among type 2 diabetes, higher PM2.5 was associated with higher HbA1c (exp[β]=1.04 [95% CI 1.01, 1.06]), lower insulin sensitivity (β=-0.42 [95% CI -0.82, -0.03]), lower insulin secretion (exp[β]=0.94 [95% CI 0.89, 0.99]), lower insulin clearance (exp[β]=0.92 [95% CI 0.87, 0.98]), higher CVD risk (exp[β]=1.07 [95% CI 0.99, 1.16]), lower V ˙ O 2 max (exp[β]=0.91 [95% CI 0.88, 0.95]), higher albuminuria (exp[β]=1.71 [95% CI 1.41, 2.08]) and higher odds of DSPN (OR 1.53 [95% CI 1.02, 2.32]). Similar associations were observed for PM10 and NO2. Associations were directionally attenuated in two-pollutant models but remained consistent in CRI and insulin-treated type 1 diabetes analyses. Differences were observed in associations between diabetes subtypes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Long-term AP exposure was consistently associated with higher HbA1c; reduced whole-body insulin sensitivity, secretion and clearance; and an increased burden of diabetes-related comorbidities in type 2 diabetes. Associations were less consistent in type 1 diabetes. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01055093.

title: Pregestational maternal diabetes primes neonatal beta cell dysfunction with structural remodelling, impaired calcium buffering and altered mTORC2-Gαq-PKCα signalling in a pig model.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Offspring of mothers with diabetes are at increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes, and this predisposition is established during fetal life. The aim of this study was to define the functional, morphological and molecular alterations in neonatal pancreatic islets associated with maternal hyperglycaemia, with a particular focus on beta cells, an area that remains poorly understood. Given its similarity to humans in endocrine pancreas development, the pig was used as a translational animal model.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using genetically diabetic and beta cell reporter pig models, we performed functional assessments of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in vivo and in situ using fresh pancreatic tissue slices from neonatal piglets born to hyperglycaemic mothers (PHGs) or normoglycaemic mothers (PNGs). Morphological and molecular profiling, including proteomics and single-cell RNA-seq, were performed to elucidate molecular changes reflecting the developmental impact of maternal diabetes on offspring metabolic health, with a particular focus on neonatal beta cells.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: PHGs were born hyperglycaemic, hyperinsulinaemic and insulin resistant, exhibiting markedly delayed glucose and insulin response curves following oral glucose administration, with more pronounced effects in male piglets. Elevated basal insulin secretion and an almost blunted glucose responsiveness of pancreatic tissue slices were associated with increased insulin and somatostatin content, expansion of beta (+35%) and delta (+47%) cell populations, and organisation into larger islet clusters. Neonatal PHG islets exhibited a molecular profile consistent with intrinsic beta cell dysfunction that partially overlapped with type 2 diabetes (e.g. RBP4 upregulation), together with alterations in glucose sensing (near absence of GLUT2), nutrient metabolism resembling congenital hyperinsulinism (HADH downregulation), and cytosolic Ca2⁺ homeostasis (near absence of the Ca2⁺ buffer calbindin D28K). In addition to an ATF4-dominated stress signature, a shift towards a distinct PHG beta cell subcluster characterised by low expression of ribosomal genes was observed, with an adaptive early-response-gene-mediated transcriptional reactivity. In contrast to the Gαs-adenylyl cyclase-cAMP-PKA signalling axis that dominated in PNG beta cells, neonatal PHG beta cells displayed distinct alterations in Gαq-PLC-PKCα signalling components, the mTORC2 target PKCα, and CREB1, suggesting a restructured signalling architecture.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Our findings reveal altered islet modelling with a unique beta cell dysfunction profile that partially overlaps with, but differs from, that of type 2 diabetes. A shift towards a beta cell subcluster exhibiting an adaptive early-response-gene-mediated transcriptional reactivity and an ATF4-associated transcriptional stress signature provides insight into molecular alterations associated with fetal exposure to maternal diabetes and may contribute to the increased risk of metabolic disease in offspring.

title: Cotransplantation With Human AAT-MSCs Enhances Human Islet Graft Survival in Humanized Mice by Modulating B- and T-Cell Responses.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Immune-mediated rejection remains a major barrier to long-term success of islet/stem cell-derived islet transplantation for type 1 diabetes. We evaluated whether cotransplantation of human islets with human α-1 antitrypsin-overexpressing mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (AAT-MSCs) improves islet graft survival by modulating human immune responses in a humanized diabetic mouse model. Humanized NOD/SCID/IL2Rγ-/- (NSG) mice were generated by irradiation and transfer of human CD34+ hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells, resulting in stable T- and B-cell reconstitution. Diabetes was induced by multiple doses of low-dose streptozotocin (STZ), after which mice received intrahepatic transplants of human islets alone or together with AAT-MSCs and were monitored for 100 days. Cotransplantation with AAT-MSCs markedly improved glycemic control, prolonged graft survival, and reduced the risk of rejection. These beneficial effects were associated with lower serum IgM levels, which inversely correlated with graft rejection, and with expansion of regulatory B cells (Bregs), followed by durable suppression of T helper 1, T helper 17, and cytotoxic T cell responses. Cotransplant grafts showed improved insulin preservation and enrichment of interleukin (IL) 10+ cells within islets. In vitro, AAT-MSCs promoted Breg differentiation, shifted cytokine production toward IL-10 over IL-6, and attenuated activated B cell-mediated cytotoxicity against human islets. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that AAT-MSC cotransplantation promotes immune tolerance and human islet graft function, supporting its translational potential to reduce reliance on systemic immunosuppression in the clinic.

abstract.label: ARTICLE HIGHLIGHTS
abstract.text: Immune-mediated rejection limits the long-term success of islet and stem cell-derived islet transplantation in type 1 diabetes, and strategies that protect the graft without systemic immunosuppression are needed. We asked whether cotransplanting human islets with α-1 antitrypsin-overexpressing mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (AAT-MSCs) improves graft outcomes in humanized mice, and how human immune responses are affected. AAT-MSC cotransplantation improved glycemic control, prolonged graft survival, and shifted immune responses toward a more regulatory, less inflammatory profile. These findings support further development of AAT-MSCs as an adjunct to reduce reliance on systemic immunosuppression in islet transplantation.

title: Transient Cognitive Vulnerability After Hypoglycemia in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: Evidence From Continuous Glucose Monitoring and Cognitive Ecologic Momentary Assessment.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Adults with type 1 diabetes experience short-term changes in cognitive performance after glycemic events; however, the duration of such cognitive effects remains unclear. We examined whether hypoglycemic and hyperglycemic events and rapid glucose changes were associated with changes in processing speed or sustained attention in adults with type 1 diabetes and whether these associations varied by time since the event.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: Participants (N = 190) completed 15 days of smartphone-based ecologic momentary assessment (EMA; 3 prompts/day) paired with continuous glucose monitoring. Cognitive performance (median reaction time and accuracy) was tested using digit symbol matching (DSM) and gradual-onset continuous performance testing (GCPT; sustained attention) by TestMyBrain (processing speed). Glycemic exposures were defined as hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia lasting ≥15 min and rapid (5-min) increases or decreases in glucose >15 mg/dL, occurring during nonoverlapping intervals: 0-1, 1-2, and 2-3 h before EMA. Multilevel models estimated associations between glycemic exposures and cognitive performance, adjusting for age, EMA count, and interruptions.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Hypoglycemic events occurring within 0-1 h of EMA were associated with slower reaction time and poorer performance on DSM and GCPT. No associations were observed for events occurring 1-2 or 2-3 h before EMA. Hyperglycemic events and rapid glucose increases or decreases were not associated with cognition across most outcomes or time windows.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Hypoglycemia was associated with a transient period of cognitive vulnerability largely confined to the hour after an event, with little evidence of delayed effects. Findings support avoiding or exercising caution during cognitively demanding tasks for up to an hour after a hypoglycemic event.

title: Clinical Guidance for Disease-Modifying Immunotherapy in Children and Adolescents With New-Onset (Stage 3) Type 1 Diabetes.
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: The 2026 U.S. approval of teplizumab, for children and adolescents aged 8-17 years with recently diagnosed stage 3 type 1 diabetes, changes the first weeks after diagnosis. Clinicians must treat hyperglycemia and teach lifelong care skills while considering whether to preserve residual β-cell function. Teplizumab is the current clinical exemplar, although the implementation challenges extend beyond one agent. This article addresses who should lead care, how to approach eligibility and timing, how to assess β-cell reserve and infection risk, how to sequence treatment with diabetic ketoacidosis recovery and early education, and how to monitor treatment safely. Teplizumab-specific recommendations are identified, with broader principles framed for adaptation across health systems.

title: Fetal, placental and amniotic fluid volume across gestation in women with type 1 diabetes: a prospective MRI study.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to compare fetal, placental and amniotic fluid volumes across gestation by use of MRI in women with type 1 diabetes and women without diabetes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective longitudinal cohort study is part of the FaPDi cohort study. The study included pregnant women with type 1 diabetes and women without diabetes who gave birth at Aalborg University Hospital between November 2020 and April 2023. All participants were invited for MRI scans at 15-20, 26-30 and 34-38 weeks' gestation, from which fetal, placental and amniotic fluid volumes were obtained. The groups were compared across gestation using multiple linear regressions and mixed-effects models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 63 pregnant women were included in the analysis (25 with type 1 diabetes and 38 without diabetes). In women with type 1 diabetes, the fetal, placental and amniotic volumes were significantly increased at visits 2 and 3. At visit 3, the adjusted differences between groups were 385.9 cm3 (95% CI 140.9, 631.0; p<0.01), 187.8 cm3 (95% CI 35.4, 340.3; p=0.02) and 420.4 cm3 (95% CI 19.5, 821.2; p=0.04) for the fetal, placental and amniotic volumes, respectively. Placental weight to birthweight ratio was increased at delivery among women with type 1 diabetes (p<0.01), but no differences in the intrauterine volume ratios were observed. Maternal HbA1c showed a positive linear correlation with all volumes at visits 2 and 3, with the strongest correlations shown for amniotic fluid volume (R2=0.36).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: MRI provides a unique insight into the intrauterine consequences of type 1 diabetes. Pregnancies complicated by type 1 diabetes are characterised by increased fetal, placental and amniotic fluid volumes. The strong association between maternal HbA1c and amniotic fluid volume suggests that amniotic fluid dynamics may provide additional insight into the intrauterine consequences of maternal glucose regulation.

title: It's All One Trial: a continuous master-protocol framework to accelerate development and confirmation of disease-modifying therapies for type 1 diabetes.
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: The time required for clinical development and regulatory approval of disease-modifying therapies for type 1 diabetes is the longest of any therapeutic area. Teplizumab, the only product that has received an accelerated approval in the USA for people with stage 3 type 1 diabetes, will require about a decade for its Phase III and confirmatory trial to be completed and full approval to be achieved. This article proposes the 'It's All One Trial' (OT) framework, a single master protocol with one continuously randomised population, one prospective statistical structure, and uninterrupted follow-up spanning early investigation, accelerated approval based on an intermediate endpoint, and later confirmation of durability and clinical benefit. The OT framework is compared with current clinical development practices for treatments aimed at preserving insulin secretion in people with recent-onset type 1 diabetes. Teplizumab's Phase III PROTECT trial and confirmatory βETA PRESERVE trials provide observed and projected timelines for late-stage development. Based on prevailing early clinical development practices and observed and projected timelines of the teplizumab trials, the OT model could reduce total development time by approximately 45 months while increasing use of participant data and reducing the need for repeated enrolment, site activation and study restarts. Implementing the OT model could shorten development timelines, lower capital barriers, conserve scarce clinical trial resources and better honour patient participation by maintaining continuous randomised follow-up, protocol-directed care and a more direct path from early biological effect to durable evidence for practice and regulation.
