title: Retatrutide, a Triple Hormone Receptor Agonist, for Treatment of Obesity.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
type_basis: PubMed研究类型：Journal Article,Randomized Controlled Trial,Clinical Trial, Phase III,Multicenter Study

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Retatrutide is a triple-receptor agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, and glucagon receptors.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this phase 3, randomized, double-blind trial, we assigned adults with obesity without diabetes to receive a once-weekly subcutaneous injection of retatrutide (at a dose of 4 mg, 9 mg, or 12 mg) or placebo for 80 weeks. Primary outcomes (evaluated in the 9-mg and 12-mg groups each vs. placebo) were the percent change in body weight and the change in the WOMAC pain score (ranging from 1 to 10, with higher scores indicating worse pain) in the subgroup of 574 participants with knee osteoarthritis and the change in the apnea-hypopnea index in the 243 participants with obstructive sleep apnea. For weight-related end points, intercurrent events were handled by a treatment-regimen estimand (intention-to-treat [ITT]). For end points in participants with knee osteoarthritis or obstructive sleep apnea, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy for intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure; ITT results are also reported.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 2339 participants underwent randomization. The mean percent change in body weight in the retatrutide groups was -17.6% (4-mg dose), -23.7% (9-mg dose), and -25.0% (12-mg dose) versus -3.9% in the placebo group (differences, -19.8 and -21.0 percentage points, respectively; P<0.001 for both comparisons). Among the participants with knee osteoarthritis, the corresponding changes in the pain score in the retatrutide groups for the hybrid estimand were -3.2, -3.5, and -3.6 versus -1.9 with placebo (differences, -1.6 and -1.8 points; both P<0.001); the corresponding changes for the ITT estimand were -3.4, -3.9, and -4.1 versus -2.5 with placebo (differences, -1.4 and -1.6 points; both P<0.001). Among the participants with obstructive sleep apnea, the corresponding changes in events per hour in the retatrutide groups for the hybrid-treatment estimand were -22.9, -34.3, and -31.7 versus -9.9 (differences, -24.4 and -21.9; both P<0.001); the corresponding changes for the ITT estimand were -22.8, -34.3, and -32.1 versus -9.6 (differences, -24.7 and -22.5; both P<0.001). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In adults with obesity, retatrutide resulted in significant weight reduction, reduced pain in participants with knee osteoarthritis, and reduced apnea-hypopnea events in participants with obstructive sleep apnea. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05929066.).

title: Cardiovascular safety of orforglipron versus insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4): a phase 3, event-driven, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority, active comparator trial.
type_basis: PubMed研究类型：Journal Article,Randomized Controlled Trial,Clinical Trial, Phase III,Multicenter Study,Equivalence Trial,Comparative Study

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Orforglipron is an oral, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. While some peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists have established cardiovascular benefit, the cardiovascular safety of non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists has not been studied. This study aimed to compare the effect of orforglipron with insulin glargine on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight who are at increased risk for cardiovascular events.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This event-driven, phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, active comparator, parallel-group study was conducted in 317 sites across 16 countries and territories. Adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk with glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) concentrations between 7·0% and 10·5% (53-91 mmol/mol) and a BMI of 25 kg/m2 or more, treated with up to three glucose-lowering medications (metformin, a sulfonylurea, and/or an SGLT2 inhibitor), were randomly assigned (1:1) to oral orforglipron maximum tolerated dose (up to 36 mg capsule [equivalent to 17·2 mg tablet]) or injectable titrated insulin glargine, each administered once daily. All participants had established cardiovascular or chronic kidney disease. The primary outcome was time to occurrence of four-component major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-4), including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for unstable angina. Non-inferiority of orforglipron to insulin glargine was declared if the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio (HR; orforglipron vs insulin glargine) was less than 1·8. The primary endpoint and other safety endpoints were assessed in all participants who took at least one dose of assigned treatment using all datapoints from baseline until withdrawal or study completion, regardless of treatment adherence. This trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05803421) and is completed.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Between May 1, 2023, and Sept 5, 2024, 2749 participants were randomly assigned (1371 to orforglipron and 1378 to insulin glargine). 1032 (38%) participants were female and 1717 (62·5%) male. 2362 (85·9%) participants had established cardiovascular disease and 1033 (37·6%) had chronic kidney disease. Mean baseline age, HbA1c, and BMI were 63·1 years (SD 9·9), 8·2% (1·0), and 33 kg/m2 (6·2), respectively. Over a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 57 (4·2%) of 1358 orforglipron participants and 67 (5·0%) of 1343 insulin glargine participants, showing non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4 (HR 0·84; 95% CI 0·59-1·20; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported in 851 (62·1%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 193 (14·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants; clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia (glucose <3 mmol/L [54 mg/dL]) occurred in 93 (6·8%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 260 (19·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants. 62 deaths were reported during the study: 19 (1·4%) of 1371 participants receiving orforglipron and 43 (3·2%) of 1355 participants receiving insulin glargine; all deaths except one (in the insulin glargine group) were deemed unrelated to treatment.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: In people with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk, the cardiovascular safety of orforglipron was confirmed by demonstrating non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent adverse event and most common reason for orforglipron treatment discontinuation with orforglipron, while clinically significant hypoglycaemia occurred less frequently with orforglipron than with insulin glargine. These findings support orforglipron as a potential once-daily, oral treatment option with established cardiovascular safety in people with type 2 diabetes and increased cardiovascular risk.

title: Survodutide Once Weekly in Adults with Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: For persons living with both type 2 diabetes and obesity, weight management may be the most effective therapy for type 2 diabetes. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists have potent weight-reducing effects, and other mechanisms may confer additional benefits. Survodutide is an investigational glucagon receptor-GLP-1 receptor dual agonist with potential weight-reducing and metabolic benefits.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this multinational, double-blind, phase 3 trial involving adults with type 2 diabetes and a body-mass index (BMI; the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of 27 or more, we randomly assigned participants in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive once-weekly subcutaneous survodutide (3.6 mg or 6.0 mg) or placebo. The two primary end points were the percent change in body weight and a reduction in body weight of at least 5% from baseline to week 76.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 752 participants (250 in the 3.6-mg survodutide group, 251 in the 6.0-mg survodutide group, and 251 in the placebo group), the mean age at baseline was 55.7 years, and the mean BMI was 36.5; 49.3% were men. The mean weight change at week 76 according to the treatment-regimen estimand (which assessed effects regardless of whether the trial regimen was discontinued or interrupted or whether other antiobesity therapies were used) was -8.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], -9.2 to -7.2) in the 3.6-mg group, -9.8% (95% CI, -10.8 to -8.8) in the 6.0-mg group, and -3.9% (95% CI, -4.9 to -2.9) in the placebo group; weight reduction of at least 5% occurred in 57.6%, 64.5%, and 35.1% of the participants, respectively (P<0.001 for all comparisons with placebo). The mean change in the glycated hemoglobin level (from a baseline level of 7.4%) was -0.9 percentage points in the 3.6-mg group, -0.8 percentage points in the 6.0-mg group, and -0.2 percentage points in the placebo group. The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal (generally mild to moderate and transient), which occurred in 182 participants (72.8%) in the 3.6-mg group, 195 (77.7%) in the 6.0-mg group, and 97 (38.6%) in the placebo group.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes, survodutide at a weekly dose of 3.6 mg or 6.0 mg resulted in significantly greater weight reduction than placebo. (Funded by Boehringer Ingelheim; SYNCHRONIZE-2 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06066528.).

title: Effects of semaglutide on kidney disease in type 2 diabetes: a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
type_basis: PubMed研究类型：Journal Article,Randomized Controlled Trial

abstract.text: The GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide preserves kidney function in people with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear. Here we report a 52-week randomized trial of subcutaneous semaglutide 1 mg once weekly versus placebo (n = 106 (n = 25 women, n = 81 men)) in participants with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease. To identify kidney-specific mechanisms of action for semaglutide, we performed integrated multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging of the kidney and biopsy for histology (n = 33), alongside single-nucleus (n = 22) and spatial transcriptomics (n = 13) on paired samples with before- and after-treatment measurements. Coprimary magnetic resonance imaging outcomes (oxygenation by R2*, global perfusion and tissue inflammation by T1 mapping) were not significantly altered by semaglutide versus placebo treatment. Secondary outcomes revealed that semaglutide treatment, as compared to placebo, was associated with a significantly reduced renal artery resistive index and stabilization of the apparent diffusion coefficient, indicating prevention of fibrosis progression. Moreover, secondary transcriptomic outcomes revealed pronounced effects of semaglutide on glomerular endothelial cells, consistent with the results of spatial analyses indicating reduced numbers of immune cells in the proximity of these endothelial cells. The results from this trial indicate that mechanisms of kidney protection by semaglutide may include reduced vascular resistance, prevention of fibrosis and improved underlying molecular programs promoting endothelial cell health. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04865770 .

title: Senolytics dasatinib and quercetin in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis: a proof-of-principle randomized, controlled trial.
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: Cellular senescence plays an important role in hepatic inflammation and fibrosis1-3. However, whether senescence represents a potential therapeutic target in humans with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) remains unexplored. Here we report the results of a phase-2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of intermittent senolytic therapy with dasatinib plus quercetin (D + Q) in participants with fibrotic MASH. Thirty-one participants (median age 56 years; 76% male; 58% with type 2 diabetes) were randomized (1:1) to receive D + Q (dasatinib 100 mg per day plus quercetin 1,000 mg per day) or placebo for three consecutive days per week over 3 weeks, repeated across three 7-week cycles. The primary endpoint, ≥1 stage fibrosis improvement without MASH worsening on paired liver biopsies, is achieved in 47% of D + Q-treated participants versus 7% with placebo (P = 0.02). MASH resolution occurs more frequently with D + Q than placebo (53% versus 7%; P = 0.02), with a greater reduction in NAFLD Activity Score (-1.43 ± 1.22 versus -0.39 ± 0.77; P = 0.012). Single-nucleus RNA sequencing demonstrates decreased senescence and fibrotic gene signatures and reduced fibrogenic cell populations in the D + Q group. Although adverse events are more frequent in the D + Q group (82% versus 43%), these are all self-limiting. Overall, this proof-of-principle trial supports the need for future trials of senolytic therapy in fibrotic MASH. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05506488 .

title: Oral small-molecule GLP-1RA safiglipron versus dapagliflozin in type 2 diabetes: a randomized, double-blind, active-comparator-controlled phase 3 trial.
type_basis: PubMed研究类型：Journal Article,Randomized Controlled Trial,Clinical Trial, Phase III,Multicenter Study

abstract.text: Safiglipron is an oral small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist administered without fasting or dietary restrictions. We evaluated its efficacy and safety versus dapagliflozin in OUTSTAND-2, a phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-comparator-controlled trial conducted at 98 sites in China. We randomized 810 adults (mean hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) 8.60%, median diabetes duration 5.0 years, 35.7% women) to safiglipron 30 mg (n = 202), safiglipron 60 mg (n = 203), safiglipron 90 mg (n = 203) or dapagliflozin 10 mg (n = 202) for 32 weeks, followed by a 20-week active-treatment extension. For the primary endpoint, treatment differences versus dapagliflozin in change from baseline in HbA1c at week 32 under the primary non-inferiority estimand were -0.30% (95% confidence interval (CI): -0.51 to -0.09), -0.22% (-0.44 to -0.01) and -0.40% (-0.62 to -0.19) for safiglipron 30 mg, 60 mg and 90 mg, respectively, establishing non-inferiority for all three doses (all P < 0.0001; non-inferiority margin 0.4%). Under the treatment policy estimand, 90 mg met the prespecified statistical criterion for superiority (difference -0.25%; 95% CI: -0.45 to -0.05; one-sided P = 0.0067), whereas 60 mg did not (P = 0.0789), after which fixed-sequence testing stopped. HbA1c target attainment rates with safiglipron versus dapagliflozin were 54.9-63.5% versus 36.5% for HbA1c <7.0% and 38.9-48.6% versus 16.1% for HbA1c ≤6.5%. Mean body weight changes were -2.35%, -3.55%, -4.17% and -3.60% for safiglipron 30 mg, safiglipron 60 mg, safiglipron 90 mg and dapagliflozin, respectively. Fasting plasma glucose, seven-point self-monitored blood glucose profiles, waist circumference, HOMA-β, HOMA-IR and changes in treatment satisfaction showed varying degrees of improvement from baseline with both safiglipron and dapagliflozin. Rescue therapy was used by 0.5-1.5% versus 0% of participants, respectively. Gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with safiglipron and mostly mild or moderate; adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 4.0%, 4.0%, 3.9% and 1.5% of participants, respectively. Safiglipron provides an effective oral treatment option for adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with metformin. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06589765 .

title: UBT251, a novel triple GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptor agonist, in adults with overweight or obesity: A multicenter, randomized phase 2 trial.
type_basis: 摘要含研究设计/结果描述，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.text: UBT251 is a novel triple agonist targeting glucagon-like peptide-1, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, and glucagon receptors. In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial, 205 adults with overweight or obesity (59.0% women; aged 18-61 years; without type 2 diabetes) received once-weekly UBT251 at 2 mg, 4 mg (initial dose 0.5 mg or 1 mg), or 6 mg, or placebo for 24 weeks. For the primary efficacy endpoint, least-squares mean percentage changes in body weight at week 24 were -19.7% to -13.6% with UBT251 vs. -2.0% with placebo; placebo-adjusted differences were -17.7% (95% confidence interval [CI], -20.8% to -14.6%) to -11.5% (95% CI, -14.1% to -9.0%; all p < 0.001). UBT251 improved waist circumference, body mass index, blood pressure, lipid profiles, and glycemic parameters. The most frequent adverse events were mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal symptoms. UBT251 produced weight reduction with cardiometabolic improvements and an acceptable safety profile, supporting phase 3 evaluation. This study was registered at China Drug Trials Registry (CTR20250288) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07177469).

title: A Microsimulation of Eligibility for Cardiorenal Combination Treatment and Potential Deaths Averted.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Clinical guidelines recommend combined use of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASi), sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP1RA) and nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (nsMRA) to reduce cardiorenal risk. However, eligibility for combination treatment and the potential effects of implementation on preventing mortality remain unclear.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a microsimulation study using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES 2007-2016 and 2017-2020). The model incorporated acute treatment effects of RASi, SGLT2i, GLP1RA, and nsMRA on estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), and serum potassium. Eligibility for combination treatment was assessed for each participant according to 73 clinical practice guideline recommendations and inclusion criteria from recently published clinical trials. Primary outcomes included: 1) the percentage of participants eligible for single or combination treatment with RASi, SGLT2i, GLP1RA, and nsMRA, and 2) the projected potential number of annually averted all-cause and cardiovascular deaths.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 8,152 adults, 15% had type 2 diabetes (DM), 14% had chronic kidney disease (CKD) and 5% had DM and CKD (DKD). Among all U.S. adults, 19% were treated with RASi, 1% with SGLT2i, 1% with GLP1RA and none with nsMRA. The dual-therapy associated with the highest eligibility was RASi+SGLT2i, with 15% of the U.S. population eligible (DM subgroup: 70%; CKD subgroup: 50%; DKD subgroup: 84%). The triple-therapy with the highest eligibility was RASi+SGLT2i+GLP1RA, with 11% overall eligibility (DM: 69%; CKD: 33%; DKD: 83%). Eligibility for quadruple-therapy was 4% overall (DM: 22%; CKD: 17%; DKD: 40%). Based on our microsimulation model, fewer individuals with diabetes were eligible for triple-therapy with RASi+SGLT2i+GLP1RA compared to dual-therapy with RASi+SGLT2i, but triple-therapy was projected to prevent 2-fold more potential all-cause and cardiovascular deaths versus dual-therapy.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Under the assumptions of our microsimulation model, eligibility for combined treatment with cardiorenal protective therapies was prevalent, particularly in adults with type 2 diabetes and/or CKD.

title: Adult Attention Deficit-Hyperactivity Disorder.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
type_basis: PubMed文献类型：Journal Article,Review

abstract.text: Attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a medical condition that is present in approximately 2.5% of adults worldwide and manifests in a variety of different ways across the lifespan. Adults with ADHD often have coexisting psychiatric disorders such as anxiety, mood, sleep, substance use, and personality disorders and are at increased risk for coexisting somatic conditions such as obesity, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and immune and inflammatory conditions. Hence, such adults may be seen by clinicians providing care for a wide range of psychiatric and somatic conditions. Nevertheless, ADHD remains unrecognized and undiagnosed in many persons. Assessment requires interviewing of the patient for core ADHD symptoms, coexisting conditions, and their functional effects, which can be facilitated by using standardized rating scales. Key components of treatment are psychoeducation and psychostimulant or nonstimulant medication, mostly in combination with psychosocial interventions and lifestyle guidance.

title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
type_basis: PubMed研究类型：Equivalence Trial,Journal Article,Multicenter Study,Randomized Controlled Trial

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. (Funded by Dexcom; CONNECT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06601166.).

title: Occupational Disparities in Cardiovascular Risk and Management in Contemporary China.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Although occupational disparities in cardiovascular health are increasingly recognized, a comprehensive understanding of cardiovascular health across contemporary occupational contexts-particularly in rapidly transitioning economies-remains limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aimed to characterize geographic and occupational patterns of cardiovascular risk, risk-factor management, and potential prevention opportunities among employed adults in contemporary China.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this nationwide cross-sectional study, we analyzed 1,421,390 employees aged 20 to 65 years who underwent health examinations at 167 centers across 24 provinces in China between 2021 and 2023. Eighteen occupations were defined based on participants' employer registration and industry affiliation, and were classified into primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors, with the tertiary sector further subclassified into modern, public, and life services. Age- and sex-standardized prevalence of coronary heart disease (CHD) and cardiometabolic risk factors was estimated, along with age- and sex-standardized rates of treatment and control for hypertension and diabetes, and treatment for hypercholesterolemia and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) control. Ten-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk was calculated using the Prediction for ASCVD Risk in China model. We then assessed changes in the proportion of individuals classified as having moderate-to-high 10-year ASCVD risk under simulated scenarios that set elevated blood pressure and total cholesterol to target levels and current smoking to noncurrent smoking and compared these reductions across occupations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean age of participants was 33.8 years, and 53.4% were male. Overall, the age- and sex-standardized prevalence of CHD was 1.33% (95% CI: 1.29%-1.37%) and demonstrated a pronounced north-south gradient (P < 0.001), with the highest in the North and the lowest in the South. Cardiometabolic risk factors also exhibited a similar geographic distribution. Employees in modern service sectors exhibited the lowest age- and sex-standardized prevalence of CHD and cardiometabolic risk factors, particularly those in "information transmission, software, and information technology," whereas the highest burdens were concentrated in the secondary sector, especially in "production and supply of electricity, heat power, gas and water." The age- and sex-standardized rates of treatment and control were 29.5% and 20.8% for hypertension, 36.6% and 21.9% for diabetes, and 17.0% and 9.5% for hypercholesterolemia treatment and LDL-C control, respectively. Modern services in the tertiary sector had the lowest treatment rates for all 3 cardiometabolic conditions and the lowest control rates for hypertension and LDL-C. Among individuals aged ≥35 years without prior ASCVD, 23.3% were classified as having moderate-to-high 10-year ASCVD risk, with marked occupational variation, highest in "agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry, and fishery" (30.4%) and lowest in "service to advanced manufacturing" (14.7%). Simulated control of elevated blood pressure, hypercholesterolemia, and current smoking revealed substantial occupational variation in potential ASCVD risk reduction.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Occupational context may provide a practical framework for identifying patterns of cardiovascular risk, management gaps, and prevention opportunities among China's working population. Despite lower observed disease burden, modern occupational sectors showed suboptimal risk-factor management, whereas simulated ASCVD risk reductions varied across occupations, highlighting distinct prevention needs and opportunities across occupational contexts.

title: Real-world, digital-first delivery of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in women.
type_basis: PubMed研究类型：Journal Article,Observational Study

abstract.text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial weight reduction and cardiometabolic benefit in randomized trials; however, prospective implementation evidence from digital care models and female sex community populations remains limited. Here we report outcomes from an observational study of 8,127 women initiating GLP-1RA therapy (99.8% tirzepatide) through a structured digital program incorporating mandatory biochemical monitoring, weekly video-supported follow-up and clinician-guided dose titration in the UK. Mean weight reduction was 16.1 kg (95% confidence interval 15.9 to 16.2; P < 0.001), representing 15.5% of baseline weight; 83.1% achieved ≥10% and 22.4% achieved ≥20% weight loss, with consistent responses across age, baseline weight and socioeconomic strata. Among participants with paired biomarker data, mean glycated hemoglobin decreased by 3.3 mmol mol-1 (95% confidence interval 3.1 to 3.4; P < 0.001), normalizing in 84.5% of those with baseline diabetes-range values and 96.3% with prediabetes, and lipid parameters improved significantly (reductions in total cholesterol of 0.77 mmol l-1, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol of 0.61 mmol l-1 and triglycerides of 0.47 mmol l-1). Retention was 91.4% at 6 months, with no serious treatment-related adverse events. These findings support the feasibility of delivering structured, digitally enabled obesity pharmacotherapy at scale and provide prospective real-world implementation evidence for this care model. Interpretation is limited by the observational design, absence of a comparator group, self-pay population and 6-month follow-up.

title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Multi-hormone Receptor Modulators for Kidney Protection in Nondiabetic Kidney Disease.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), together with newer multi-hormone receptor modulators that target glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon and amylin, have emerged as promising therapies for chronic kidney disease. This review examines the mechanisms through which these agents may protect the kidney and summarizes the emerging clinical evidence in populations without diabetes. Kidney protection appears to arise through complementary direct and indirect routes. Direct effects include natriuresis through inhibition of the sodium-hydrogen exchanger (NHE)-3, modulation of glomerular hemodynamics through effects on afferent arteriolar tone and vasoconstrictor pathways, and attenuation of renal inflammation; mechanisms that are largely independent of glucose lowering. Indirect mechanisms include reductions in the metabolic, hemodynamic and cardiac burden on the kidney through weight loss, blood pressure lowering, and improvement of heart failure. Beyond selective GLP-1R-agonism, the added hormonal components of multi-hormone receptor modulators engage distinct physiological pathways whose interactions may be additive, synergistic or counteracting, but remain incompletely understood. The efficacy of GLP-1 RAs and multi-hormone receptor modulators in people without diabetes is currently supported by results from secondary kidney endpoints in phase-3 obesity and cardiovascular outcome trials, including reductions in albuminuria and preservation of estimated glomerular filtration rate. Several dedicated outcome studies of GLP-1 RAs and multi-hormone receptor modulators are now underway and will determine whether these therapies become a new pillar of care in nondiabetic kidney disease.

title: The Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study measured hepcidin, cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic outcomes in chronic kidney disease.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Abnormal iron homeostasis plays a critical role in extra-hematopoietic disorders. The relationship of hepcidin, the master iron regulator, to clinical outcomes, has not been characterized in a large cohort of chronic kidney disease (CKD).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: To determine if plasma hepcidin level predicts cardiovascular (CV), kidney, and metabolic outcomes in patients with CKD, we studied 3826 patients enrolled in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study. Hazard ratios for hepcidin tertiles were estimated from Cox Proportional Hazards regression for primary outcomes of incident heart failure (HF), end stage kidney disease (kidney failure) or halving of the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and new onset diabetes or prediabetes. Secondary outcomes included atherosclerotic events and all-cause and CV mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The median and interquartile range of plasma hepcidin level was 43 (22, 77) ng/mL. Higher plasma hepcidin levels were associated with older age, male sex, non-Hispanic Black race, diabetes, lower eGFR, higher albuminuria, increased plasma levels of iron indices, C-terminal fibroblast growth factor 23, and markers of inflammation (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein and interleukin-6). We found no association between plasma hepcidin level and the risk for incident HF or prediabetes/diabetes. However, compared to the middle tertile, the highest hepcidin tertile was independently associated with increased risk for kidney outcomes (hazard ratio 1.19; 95% confidence interval 1.09, 1.30) and atherosclerotic events (hazard ratio 1.34; 95% confidence interval 1.09, 1.64), while the lowest hepcidin tertile was associated with increased risk for all-cause and CV mortality in fully adjusted multivariable models including iron indices and inflammation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Both low and high plasma levels of hepcidin are associated with adverse clinical outcomes.

title: Safety outcomes of semaglutide by chronic kidney disease severity in the FLOW trial.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: People with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) often experience medication intolerance and side effects that worsen with lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). This prespecified secondary analysis assessed the safety of semaglutide by baseline eGFR.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: FLOW (NCT03819153) was a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial testing the efficacy of subcutaneous semaglutide 1.0 mg once-weekly on a primary kidney outcome (50% or more eGFR reduction, kidney failure, or death due to kidney or cardiovascular causes) in participants with T2D and CKD. Safety data were collected selectively and included serious adverse events (SAEs), AEs leading to treatment discontinuation, and prespecified AEs of special interest (AESIs). In this descriptive assessment, systematically collected safety data were reported numerically by baseline eGFR.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 3533 participants, 1767 received semaglutide and 1766 received placebo. Fewer SAEs were reported with semaglutide than placebo across baseline eGFR subgroups (45.1% versus 50.4% in the 60 or more ml/min per 1.73 m2 subgroup, and 56.4% versus 60.4% in the under 30 ml/min per 1.73 m2 subgroup). SAEs related to infections and infestations; cardiac disorders; respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal disorders; and metabolism and nutrition disorders were generally less frequent with semaglutide than placebo, regardless of baseline eGFR. Treatment discontinuations due to AEs were higher with lower baseline eGFR across treatment groups (60 or more ml/min per 1.73 m2: semaglutide 11.2%, placebo 11.3%; under 30 ml/min per 66 1.73 m2: semaglutide 18.8%, placebo 18.7%). Discontinuations specifically due to gastrointestinal AEs were reported more frequently with semaglutide (4.5%) than placebo (1.1%), regardless of baseline eGFR. Frequencies of AESI were similar between treatment groups across baseline eGFR subgroups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this safety assessment, SAEs were reported less frequently with semaglutide than placebo, with corresponding patterns observed for treatment discontinuations and AESIs. No unexpected safety concerns were identified across the spectrum of eGFR represented in the FLOW trial.

title: Retatrutide Once Weekly for Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide 1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for treating obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In two phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials nested within larger basket trials of once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide, we assigned adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and a body-mass index (the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of at least 27, without (TRIUMPH-1-OSA) or with (TRIUMPH-2-OSA) type 2 diabetes, to receive retatrutide (4, 9, or 12 mg) or placebo. The primary end point was the change in the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, the average number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep) at 80 weeks with 9 mg and 12 mg of retatrutide. For OSA-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy used for participants who had intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy used elsewhere. We also report intention-to-treat (ITT) results.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 243 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and 448 in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The baseline mean AHI was 58.6 and 55.9 events per hour, respectively, and the mean body weight was 119.6 and 115.9 kg. At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the AHI (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OSA were -22.9 (4 mg), -34.3 (9 mg), and -31.7 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -9.9 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -13.0 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -23.0 to -3.0], -24.4 [95% CI, -34.1 to -14.7], and -21.9 [95% CI, -32.2 to -11.5], respectively). The changes with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-2-OSA were -19.2 (4 mg), -24.7 (9 mg), and -25.4 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -10.3 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -8.9 [95% CI, -15.9 to -2.0], -14.4 [95% CI, -21.6 to -7.2], and -15.1 [95% CI, -22.5 to -7.7]). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -13.2 (95% CI, -22.6 to -3.9), -24.7 (95% CI, -34.1 to -15.3), and -22.5 (95% CI, -31.9 to -13.1) in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -8.8 (95% CI, -15.8 to -1.7), -13.9 (95% CI, -21.3 to -6.6), and -15.0 (95% CI, -22.5 to -7.4) in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The mean percent change in body weight with retatrutide (key secondary end point) was -12.5 to -22.2% in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -12.1 to -18.5% in TRIUMPH-2-OSA, versus -4.8% and -5.6% with placebo (treatment-regimen estimand). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In adults with OSA and obesity or overweight with or without type 2 diabetes, retatrutide resulted in significantly greater decreases in the AHI than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-1 and -2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05929066 and NCT05929079.).

title: Obesity in Children Aged 2 to 12 Years: A Review.
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Obesity affects 15% of children aged 2 to 5 years and 22% of children aged 6 to 11 years in the US. Obesity in children is associated with dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and obstructive sleep apnea. Compared with normal-weight peers, children with obesity have lower quality of life and are 5 times more likely to have obesity in adulthood.

abstract.label: OBSERVATIONS
abstract.text: Body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) is used to identify children at risk for excess adiposity, and guidelines recommend that clinicians screen for obesity using BMI starting at age 2 years. Among children, obesity is defined using standardized age- and sex-specific growth charts, with obesity defined as BMI in the 95th or higher percentile and severe obesity as BMI of 120% or greater of the 95th percentile. Obesity treatment in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, consisting of at least 26 contact hours of face-to-face group or family-based activities that incorporate nutrition, physical activity, and behavior change education delivered to the child and caregivers over a 3- to 12-month period. Intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment reduces BMI by 0.7 compared with children who do not participate in intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment. The only obesity pharmacotherapy currently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for children younger than 12 years is setmelanotide, a melanocortin-4 receptor agonist, which is indicated for 3 forms of rare monogenic obesity (LEPR, POMC, and PCSK1 genetic variants), Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and acquired hypothalamic obesity. Liraglutide is currently only FDA approved for youth aged 12 years or older; however, a randomized clinical trial among children aged 6 to younger than 12 years demonstrated that, compared with placebo, liraglutide reduced BMI by 7.4%. Metabolic and bariatric surgery is rarely used in children younger than age 12 years and evidence supporting its use in children is limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: Obesity in children is associated with chronic disease, such as hypertension, and with poor quality of life. Evidence-based treatment for obesity in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, and pharmacotherapy may provide additional benefit, although short- and long-term safety and efficacy data are limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.

title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use and Levels of Hemoglobin, Markers of Iron Metabolism, and Erythropoiesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: In randomized clinical trials, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was associated with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit compared with placebo. However, the magnitude and importance of this association remain unclear.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and levels of hemoglobin, hematocrit, and markers of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis compared with placebo or active comparator.

abstract.label: DATA SOURCES
abstract.text: PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 22, 2026.

abstract.label: STUDY SELECTION
abstract.text: Randomized, double-masked clinical trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitor use with placebo or active comparators in patients with 1 or more of the following conditions: cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease.

abstract.label: DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS
abstract.text: Three reviewers independently extracted data and results were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: Primary outcomes were changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Secondary outcomes were changes in red blood cell concentration, erythropoietin (EPO), and iron measures (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hepcidin).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 85 randomized clinical trials were analyzed (median [IQR] duration, 24 [12-32] weeks), including 70 543 participants (mean [SD] age, 62.4 [9.4] years; 25 334 female [35.9%]). Mean (SD) baseline hemoglobin was 13.6 (1.5) g/dL; baseline hematocrit was 41.5% (4.9). Seventy-eight clinical trials (67 208 participants) compared SGLT2 inhibitors with placebo, and 7 clinical trials (3335 participants) used active comparators, most commonly sitagliptin (2 trials [1158 participants]). From baseline to follow-up, hemoglobin changed by 0.55 g/dL (95% CI, 0.49 to 0.61 g/dL; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group, and -0.08 g/dL (95% CI, -0.13 to -0.03 g/dL; P = .003) in the control group (difference, 0.60 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.66 g/dL; P < .001). From baseline to follow-up, hematocrit changed by 2.17% (95% CI, 1.95% to 2.39%; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group and -0.13% (95% CI, -0.28% to 0.01%; P = .07) in the control group (difference, 2.36%; 95% CI, 2.19% to 2.52%; P < .001). Of the 6 secondary outcomes, 4 showed significant associations with SGLT2 inhibitors, including increased EPO (2.35 mIU/mL in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs 0.04 mIU/mL in control group; difference, 2.11 mIU/mL [95% CI, 0.5-3.71 mIU/mL]; P = .01) and decreased transferrin saturation (-2.2% in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs -0.10% in control group; difference, -0.84% [95% CI, -1.21% to -0.47%]; P < .001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, compared with control, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with small statistically significant increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. The clinical significance of these findings is unclear.

title: Empagliflozin Therapy in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: KEY POINTS
abstract.text: Empagliflozin 25 mg once daily for 12 months was safe and well tolerated in adults with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease at high risk of rapid progression. Those randomized to empagliflozin had a greater rate of increase in total kidney volume over 12 months compared with placebo. There was no difference between groups in the chronic rate of change in eGFR, nor in change in vascular stiffness, symptoms, and copeptin.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors reduce the risk of diabetic and nondiabetic kidney disease progression; however, their safety and efficacy in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) are undetermined.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this pilot and feasibility randomized controlled trial, we assigned 50 participants, 18-55 years of age, with ADPKD, at high risk of progression, not treated with tolvaptan, to receive empagliflozin (25 mg once daily) or placebo in a 1:1 ratio for 12 months. Primary outcomes were medication safety and tolerability. Secondary outcomes were ( 1 ) change in height-adjusted total kidney volume; ( 2 ) acute and chronic slope of eGFR; and ( 3 ) changes in aortic pulse wave velocity, plasma copeptin levels, urine kidney injury molecule-1, and patient-reported outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean age was 42±7 years, and eGFR was 70±17 ml/min per 1.73 m 2 . Frequency of adverse events was similar between the 2 groups. Urinary tract infection occurred in 2 empagliflozin-treated patients versus none in placebo and AKI in 1 placebo-treated patient. In total, 96% of the participants in each group tolerated the full dose of the study drug. Among the secondary outcomes, rate of change in height-adjusted total kidney volume was significantly greater in empagliflozin-treated participants (10.5%/yr; 95% confidence interval, 8.2% to 12.7%) compared with placebo (5.1%/yr; 95% confidence interval, 3.0% to 7.3%; P = 0.001). There was a faster acute decline in eGFR at 1 month among the empagliflozin (-6.2 ml/min per 1.73 m 2 ) versus placebo groups (0.1 ml/min per 1.73 m 2 ; P = 0.01), but no differences in eGFR change from 1 to 12 months (empagliflozin group: -0.77±1.44 ml/min per 1.73 m 2 per year versus placebo group: -2.87±1.96 ml/min per 1.73 m 2 per year; P = 0.4). No between-group differences were observed in changes in aortic pulse wave velocity, copeptin, urine kidney injury molecule-1, and ADPKD Impact Score.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Empagliflozin at 25 mg once daily was well tolerated by patients with ADPKD. Empagliflozin induced an expected acute decline in eGFR by 1 month, followed by stable eGFR. However, those treated with empagliflozin had a greater increase in kidney volume.

title: UBT251, a novel triple GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptor agonist, in adults with type 2 diabetes: A multicenter, randomized phase 2 trial.
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: This phase 2 trial included 211 Chinese participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus (mean age 48.4 years; 131 participants were male). Participants received once-weekly subcutaneous UBT251 (2 mg, 4 mg [initial dose 0.5 mg], 4 mg [initial dose 1 mg], or 6 mg), 1 mg semaglutide, or placebo for 24 weeks. At week 24, UBT251 achieved least-squares mean changes in glycated hemoglobin of -2.16% (95% CI, -2.39 to -1.92) to -1.98% (95% CI, -2.31 to -1.64), versus -1.77% (95% CI, -1.99 to -1.54) for semaglutide and -0.66% (95% CI, -0.90 to -0.41) for placebo (placebo-adjusted differences: -1.50% to -1.32%; all p < 0.001). UBT251 significantly reduced fasting blood glucose, 2-h postprandial glucose, and waist circumference versus placebo (all p < 0.001). Weight reduction with UBT251 was significantly greater than both placebo and semaglutide (all p < 0.05). Gastrointestinal events were the most common treatment-emergent adverse events. These findings support further phase 3 evaluation of UBT251. Registration: CTR20250029; NCT07163624.

title: Metabolic heterogeneity of obesity.
type_basis: PubMed文献类型：Journal Article,Review

abstract.text: Multi-organ-system insulin resistance is the key pathogenic driver of obesity-related metabolic complications and diseases, such as atherogenic dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes. However, there is considerable heterogeneity in insulin sensitivity among people with obesity. Some are considered to have metabolically healthy obesity, with normal insulin sensitivity in conjunction with normal fasting blood glucose, oral glucose tolerance, plasma lipid profile and intrahepatic triglyceride content. In this Review, we discuss metabolic differences at the cellular, organ-system and systemic levels between people with metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity; we also discuss heterogeneity in the therapeutic effects of weight reduction. A better understanding of the differences between metabolically divergent groups and the physiological responses to weight loss can help identify the factors responsible for the link between excess adiposity and metabolic dysfunction and disease.

title: Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in ISCHEMIA-EXTEND.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: It is unknown whether routine invasive management of chronic coronary disease improves long-term survival when added to guideline-directed medical therapy.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To compare the effects of initial invasive and conservative strategies on long-term mortality in patients with chronic coronary disease.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: In this long-term follow-up study of the International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness with Medical and Invasive Approaches (ISCHEMIA), an international trial of patients with chronic coronary disease, moderate or severe ischemia, left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or more, and no left main coronary artery disease, unacceptable angina, or recent acute coronary syndrome, participants were randomized at 320 sites in 37 countries beginning August 2012 and followed up through December 2025. Data were analyzed using the intention-to-treat principle.

abstract.label: INTERVENTION
abstract.text: ISCHEMIA randomized patients to an initial invasive strategy of guideline-directed medical therapy plus coronary angiography and revascularization (when feasible) or an initial conservative strategy with guideline-directed medical therapy alone, with invasive management for failure of medical therapy.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: All-cause, cardiovascular, and noncardiovascular mortality were analyzed using cumulative incidence estimates, Cox and Fine-Gray models, bayesian analysis, and restricted mean survival time.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 5179 participants, median age was 64 (IQR, 58-70) years; 23% were female, 42% had diabetes, and median ejection fraction was 60% (IQR, 55%-65%). During 9-year median follow-up (range, 1 day to 13.4 years), 1071 deaths occurred (782 during extended follow-up): 672 cardiovascular, 359 noncardiovascular, and 40 unclassified. All-cause 11-year mortality was not significantly different between groups (25.8% invasive vs 26.9% conservative; estimated difference, -1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -4.2 to 2.1 percentage points]; adjusted hazard ratio [AHR], 0.97 [95% CI, 0.86-1.09]). By bayesian analysis, the posterior probability of more than 1 percentage-point survival benefit to invasive vs conservative was low (18%). Cardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 15.8% in the invasive group vs 17.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, -1.4 percentage points [95% CI, -4.0 to 1.3 percentage points]; AHR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.75-1.02]). Noncardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 9.1% in the invasive group vs 8.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, 1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -0.9 to 2.9 percentage points]; AHR, 1.18 [95% CI, 0.96-1.45]). Eleven-year restricted mean survival was not significantly different (estimated difference, 14 days [95% CI, -41 to 70 days]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this study, long-term all-cause mortality in patients with high-risk chronic coronary disease was not significantly different after routine invasive vs initial conservative management.

abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04894877.

title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Uncertainty persists regarding the effects of intensive blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in Brazil, patients with elevated blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and high cardiovascular risk received intensive therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or standard therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 9476 ethnically diverse patients who were enrolled, 4745 were assigned to receive intensive therapy and 4731 to receive standard therapy. The mean (±SD) age was 64.7±8.2 years, and 5871 of the patients (62.0%) were women. The mean systolic blood pressure during follow-up (with exclusion of the first 3 months) was 121.8±10.8 mm Hg in the intensive-therapy group and 135.4±8.2 mm Hg in the standard-therapy group. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years (interquartile range, 3.9 to 4.0), a primary-outcome event occurred in 286 patients (6.0%; 1.65 events per 100 person-years) in the intensive-therapy group and in 315 patients (6.7%; 1.83 events per 100 person-years) in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.77 to 1.06; P = 0.20). Serious adverse events occurred in 706 patients (14.9%) with intensive therapy and in 693 patients (14.6%) with standard therapy.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among patients with type 2 diabetes, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared with less than 140 mm Hg, did not reduce the occurrence of major cardiovascular events. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-DIABETES ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04040634.).

title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for the treatment of painful knee osteoarthritis in persons with obesity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In two phase 3 trials, adults without diabetes who had painful knee osteoarthritis and a body-mass index of at least 27 were randomly assigned to receive once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide (9 or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-4 and 4, 9, or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-1-OA) or placebo. In TRIUMPH-4, the primary end points were the change in the WOMAC pain score (range, 0 to 10, with higher scores indicating worse pain) and the percent change in body weight at week 68. In TRIUMPH-1-OA, the primary end point was the change in the WOMAC pain score at week 80. For non-pain-related end points, intercurrent events were handled with a treatment-policy strategy. For pain-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy for intercurrent events that suggested treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy elsewhere. We also report results for an intention-to-treat (ITT) estimand.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 445 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-4 and 574 in TRIUMPH-1-OA. At 68 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-4 were -3.96 (9 mg) and -3.74 (12 mg), versus -2.12 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.83 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -2.37 to -1.30] and -1.61 [95% CI, -2.16 to -1.07], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -1.70 (95% CI, -2.19 to -1.22) and -1.38 (95% CI, -1.91 to -0.85) (P<0.001 for all comparisons). The mean percent changes in body weight with retatrutide were -20.0% (9 mg) and -23.7% (12 mg), versus -4.6% with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -15.4 percentage points [95% CI, -18.7 to -12.1] and -19.2 percentage points [95% CI, -22.4 to -15.9]; P<0.001 for both comparisons). At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OA were -3.22 (4 mg), -3.48 (9 mg), and -3.64 (12 mg), versus -1.87 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.35 [95% CI, -1.92 to -0.78], -1.61 [95% CI, -2.20 to -1.02], and -1.77 [95% CI, -2.34 to -1.20], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -0.96 (95% CI, -1.61 to -0.30), -1.41 (95% CI, -2.07 to -0.75), and -1.64 (95% CI, -2.26 to -1.02) (P≤0.005 for all comparisons). In both trials, serious adverse events were more common with retatrutide than with placebo, and the most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In participants with painful knee osteoarthritis and obesity, treatment with retatrutide resulted in significantly greater reductions in both the WOMAC pain score and body weight than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-4 and -1 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05931367 and NCT05929066.).

title: Metabolic Unloading: How SGLT2i Recalibrate Cell Energetics to Slow CKD Progression.
type_basis: 仅Journal Article不足以确认原创研究；待复核

abstract.text: Kidney outcome trials demonstrate that sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors consistently slow chronic kidney disease progression; however, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely defined, as benefits extend beyond glycemic control and hemodynamic effects across diabetic and non-diabetic chronic kidney disease. This review advances a unifying framework in which metabolic unloading of the proximal tubule contributes to renoprotection. The metabolic burden of solute reabsorption places the proximal tubule at the center of renal energetics, predisposing it to hypoxia, mitochondrial stress, and maladaptive injury responses. We synthesize evidence that these agents reduce adenosine triphosphate-dependent transport workload, oxygen consumption and may also reduce megalin-dependent endocytosis, with downstream effects on mitochondrial efficiency, redox balance, and autophagy/mitophagy supported by emerging preclinical data. By mitigating energetic stress, these agents divert tubular cell fate away from maladaptive hypertrophy and fibrosis toward adaptive repair. This framework integrates spatial cortex-medulla vulnerability, reconciles early hemodynamic changes with durable slowing of estimated glomerular filtration rate decline, and explores disease-agnostic benefit. We discuss translational implications including early initiation, identification of high workload phenotypes (hyperfiltration, recovery after acute kidney injury), and deployment of energetics associated biomarkers such as ketones, oxidative stress profiles, and estimated glomerular filtration rate slope. This review positions cellular energetics as an important upstream constraint shaping kidney disease progression, offering a foundation for nephroprotective strategies.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure in Patients Considered Unsuitable for Oral Anticoagulation: Randomized Outcomes Through 5 Years in ASAP-TOO.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) use in atrial fibrillation is suboptimal due to real or perceived bleeding risks. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an alternative to OAC, but pivotal trials used OAC comparators.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The study sought to assess the long-term safety and effectiveness of LAAC in patients deemed unsuitable for OAC.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The ASAP-TOO trial was a multinational randomized trial of patients with atrial fibrillation, CHA2DS2-VASc (congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 years, diabetes mellitus, prior stroke or transient ischemic attack or thromboembolism, vascular disease, age 65-74 years, sex category) score ≥2, and OAC unsuitability; target enrollment was 888 patients. Patients were assigned 2:1 to LAAC with a Watchman device or control treatment-single antiplatelet therapy or no therapy. Device patients received dual antiplatelet therapy for 3 months and aspirin through 12 months. The primary effectiveness endpoint was ischemic stroke or systemic embolism; the primary safety endpoint was death, ischemic stroke, systemic embolism, or 7-day device/procedure-related events requiring major intervention.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Enrollment stopped early because of slow accrual, accentuated by the COVID-19 pandemic: only 481 patients were randomized (320 LAAC, 161 control treatment) and withdrawal was significant (7.8% LAAC, 24.2% control treatment), with disparate follow-up durations (median 876 days and 440.1 total patient-years of follow-up for control patients; median 1,768 days and 1,154.6 total patient-years of follow-up for LAAC patients), reducing statistical power. Patients were 75 ± 8 years of age, the CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.6 ± 1.7, and 34% had prior intracranial/subdural hemorrhage. Implantation success was 97.8%. Only 31 of the 101 planned primary effectiveness events occurred, fewer than the 34 events required to trigger the first planned interim analysis. The primary safety endpoint occurred in 1.0% of implant-attempted patients, meeting the prespecified performance goal (P < 0.0001); there were 3 pericardial effusions requiring intervention. At up to 5 years, ischemic stroke or systemic embolism occurred in 7.8% with LAAC and 11.4% with control treatment (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.35-1.52; P = 0.39). Major bleeding was 22.1% with LAAC and 15.7% with control treatment (HR: 1.64; 95% CI: 0.96-2.81; P = 0.067), concentrated during the first 3 months. In an exploratory analysis, disabling/fatal stroke was nominally less frequent with LAAC (2.2% vs 5.7%; HR: 0.32; 95% CI: 0.10-1.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this prematurely terminated and underpowered trial, LAAC implantation was successful, with acceptable safety. Long-term estimates with LAAC were numerically favorable for thromboembolism but imprecise, while early bleeding was increased with the mandated antiplatelet regimen. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory and integrated with contemporary evidence and shared decision making. (Assessment of the WATCHMAN Device in Patients Unsuitable for Oral Anticoagulation [ASAP-TOO]; NCT02928497).

title: Once-Weekly Ribupatide for Weight Loss in Adults in China With Overweight or Obesity: The GEMINI-1 Randomized Clinical Trial.
type_basis: 结构化方法/结果摘要，原创候选待人工复核

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Obesity is a major health problem in China; more pharmacotherapy choices for long-term weight management are needed.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, for weight loss in adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial was conducted at 55 sites in China. From May to June 2024, adults without diabetes who had a body mass index of 28 or greater or 24 or greater with at least 1 weight-related comorbidity were enrolled, with final follow-up on June 20, 2025.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: Participants were randomized to receive once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide (target doses of 2 mg, 4 mg, or 6 mg) or matching placebo for 48 weeks, with dose escalation for up to 20 weeks and concomitant lifestyle intervention.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: The primary outcome was change in body weight from baseline to week 48, including percent change in body weight and the percentage of participants achieving at least 5% body weight reduction, analyzed under the treatment policy estimand.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 567 randomized participants (309 [54.5%] female; mean [SD] age was 34.4 [8.4] years, body weight was 93.0 [17.3] kg, and body mass index was 33.3 [4.5]), 514 (90.7%) completed the 48-week treatment period. Least-squares mean percentage changes in body weight at week 48 were -10.7%, -16.4%, and -17.7% with ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg, respectively, vs -1.4% with placebo. At week 48, the placebo-adjusted differences in percentage change in body weight were -9.3 (95% CI, -11.4 to -7.3) percentage points with ribupatide 2 mg, -15.0 (95% CI, -17.1 to -12.9) percentage points with ribupatide 4 mg, and -16.3 (95% CI, -18.4 to -14.2) percentage points with ribupatide 6 mg (P < .001 for all). For at least 5% body weight reduction at week 48, the multiply imputed response rates were 68.1% (95% CI, 59.9% to 75.3%) for ribupatide 2 mg (97 of 142), 88.0% (95% CI, 81.3% to 92.6%) for ribupatide 4 mg (124 of 141), 85.7% (95% CI, 78.6% to 90.7%) with ribupatide 6 mg (121 of 141), and 16.0% (95% CI, 10.8% to 23.1%) with placebo (23 of 143). Placebo-adjusted differences for ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg were 52.0 (95% CI, 42.2 to 61.9), 72.0 (95% CI, 63.7 to 80.2), and 69.7 (95% CI, 61.1 to 78.3) percentage points, respectively (all P < .001). The most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events with ribupatide were gastrointestinal events, occurring in 47.9%, 58.2%, and 63.1% of participants receiving ribupatide 2 mg, 4 mg, and 6 mg, respectively, compared with 23.1% receiving placebo; most were mild to moderate in severity and few participants (0.7%) permanently discontinued study treatment because of adverse events.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: Among adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes, once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide resulted in significantly greater weight loss at 48 weeks. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent tolerability findings.
